packages/chord/test/delta-benchmark/memory-benchmark.worker.ts -- benchmark worker
packages/chord/test/delta-traversal.bench.ts -- vitest bench, not a test
tasks.notes:
Native ports have no Proxy, so Draft<T> becomes an explicit mutation API over node handles.
Rust: `change.state()` returns a DraftObject/DraftArray/DraftValue view with get/set/delete/keys/len, the array mutators (push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, reverse, sort_by, fill, copy_within) and string helpers (append, set_text).
Go: the same as methods on *DraftNode.
These API calls must update the same internal structures as the JS Proxy traps, so the emitted ops match exactly. Tests assert exact op arrays, such as ["t",["text"],3] and ["a",["text"],"xyz"].

Port the following exactly:
- The piece-table treap: base and insert pieces with step +/-1.
- The xorshift priority generator seeded with 0x9e3779b9. Use u32 wrapping arithmetic to reproduce JS `>>>0`, `<<` and `^` on int32 (Rust: wrapping ops; Go: uint32).
- The emission order: remove runs, then the permutation (m), then insert runs, then overrides.
- Dense-region detection: at least 256 candidates at density 50% or more.
- MAX_DELTA_OPERATIONS 4096 and MAX_SIMPLE_OBJECT_NODES 128, both falling back to r.
- The rule that a mutation under a reserved key folds into an s op on the nearest safe ancestor.

Materialization uses applyImmutableTrusted, except batches containing p or m, which go through applyImmutable. Untouched subtrees must stay shared (Arc / pointer identity), because diff identity anchors and tests rely on it.

clonePlacement validates placed values through copyJson (alias-free). Natively, values are immutable and shared, so the placement copy can become structural sharing, but validation (non-finite numbers) must remain.

Change lifecycle
Status is open, prepared, consumed, aborted or stale. Reusing a stale handle must throw with the same messages. Do not port the WeakRef context registry with its prune budget of 256 literally:
- Rust: Weak<RefCell<ContextState>> or generation ids in an arena.
- Go: an epoch counter on the tracker, with handles holding the epoch and checking it. Go 1.24 weak.Pointer is optional.

Test porting
tracker.test.ts (1454 lines) has many JS-only cases: property descriptors, prototype behaviour, Reflect and generic receivers, valueOf coercion order, `then` lookups, isProxy, Array.isArray, and JSON.stringify through the proxy. Skip those subcases. Port lifecycle, emission, safety, splice/permutation, text and root-array cases.
In delta-apply-immutable.test.ts, skip the Object.keys monkeypatch and frozen-object cases.
In delta-clone.test.ts and state-value.test.ts, skip the isFrozen, accessor and null-prototype parts; keep the alias-freedom and validation parts.
state-fuzz.test.ts uses a seeded mulberry32 PRNG with seeds 1..100: `seed=(seed+0x6d2b79f5)|0`, Math.imul. Port the PRNG exactly so the fuzz sequences match.

tasks.title: Chord replicated state, wire parsers/codec, RemoteServiceProvider and endpoint
tasks.notes:
The tests import the replicatedState() and defineService() helpers from src/index.ts, which lives in api.ts in chord-services-consumer-facets. Natively, either build MutableReplicatedState and Service tokens directly in the tests, or define those two constructors in this unit's module.

State delivery semantics
- Publisher sequence 0 is the hydrate.
- Publications go into a FIFO queue; a publish from inside a listener is queued, not nested.
- Exact-source listeners are called synchronously.
- Public subscribers have a 100-entry pending cap. On overflow the queue keeps an unstarted hydration plus the newest delivery.
- Async listeners deliver one at a time.
- Errors go to onError, otherwise they are rethrown from a queueMicrotask.
- MutableReplicatedStateImpl.change rejects reentrancy and a PromiseLike return with a TypeError, and does not publish when the change is a no-op.
- AttachedReplicatedStateImpl fails and disposes when it detects a cursor gap.
- ReplicatedStateReplica:
  - Hydrate requires a base batch.
  - Update requires sequence+1; otherwise it clears and throws.
  - Every revision is validated.

Rust
These semantics assume a single-threaded event loop. Run them on a tokio current_thread runtime with a LocalSet and Rc<RefCell> registries, or use Arc<Mutex> with care that locks are never held across listener calls. Model the microtask rethrow as an error sink.

Go
Use a mutex-protected publisher with a goroutine per async subscriber drain.

The JS tests flush microtasks with `await Promise.resolve()`. Rewrite them with explicit flush or yield helpers, or with channels and wait-for.

state-internals.ts is a WeakMap registry from a state object to its internals (snapshot, subscribe). Natively, ReplicatedState is a concrete type that exposes internals through a crate-private trait (Rust) or an unexported interface (Go).

Provider
- Subscription:
  - The snapshot is atomic; updates buffer until activate().
  - Update 101 replaces the queue with {type:"reset",snapshot}.
  - snapshotSequences suppresses updates already covered by the snapshot.
- Keyed generations increase per key.
- Keyed snapshot instances are sorted with localeCompare. This needs ICU root collation: icu_collator (Rust), golang.org/x/text/collate with language.Und (Go).
- Member classification uses Object.keys(impl).sort(), which sorts by UTF-16 code units. Natively, implementations register an explicit member table (name to Method(async fn(args, ctx)) or State(handle)) sorted by UTF-16 code-unit order.
- invoke appends the Context as a trailing argument.
- createRemoteServiceEndpoint swallows publish failures.

Wire
- The control serviceId is "$chord.service", with members catalogue, subscribe ([subscriptionId, serviceId, mode]) and unsubscribe.
- Parsers use exact key sets and their error messages are asserted. Parse from a generic JSON value rather than relying on serde/encoding/json struct decoding.
- Integer rules: update sequence >= 1, snapshot sequence >= 0, generation >= 1.
- A reset must contain exactly one r op per member.

Serialization field order is part of the wire format and must be preserved:
- ServiceCall: {serviceId, instance?, member, args}
- update: {type, instance?, member, sequence, ops}
- snapshot: {serviceId, mode, instances:[{instance?, members:[{name, kind, sequence, ops}]}]}
Optional fields are omitted, never null. In Rust, use declared field order with skip_serializing_if. In Go, use struct field order with omitempty, or a custom marshaller where a zero value is legal.

state-codec
The codec registry key is JSON.stringify([key??null, generation??null, member]); a tuple key works natively. Codecs reset on snapshot, reset, replaced and unavailable. On closed, only that instance's codecs are removed.

tasks.title: Chord service consumer binding, service slots, instance directory, FacetKernel host and public API
skipped_tests: packages/chord/test/services.test.ts (case 'checks remote JSON contracts only at compile time') -- uses @ts-expect-error to check TS types; natively this is enforced by trait bounds or has no equivalent
tasks.notes:
Consumer facades
In JS these are dynamic Proxies: methods are callable MemberSlots that require a trailing Context, and state members expose .value and .subscribe.
Rust: a RemoteServiceHandle with `call(member, Vec<Value>, &Context) -> impl Future<Output=Result<Value>>` and `state(member) -> StateView`. Add a macro (for example chord_service!) that generates typed wrappers per contract.
Go: a *RemoteFacade with Call(ctx, member, args...) and State(member).
Facades must stay stable across rebind and provider replacement. They are cleared on unavailable or disconnect, and later access throws the same RemoteServiceError codes. isContext is a duck-type check for the trailing argument; natively the argument is typed.

KeyedBinding uses revision fencing: an update with a stale generation is dropped. InstanceDirectory runs one observer task per instance under withCancel(BACKGROUND) and reports errors only if that context was not aborted. In Rust, use a tokio task with a CancellationToken. In Go, use a goroutine with context.WithCancel.

ready() loops until the readiness revision is stable. dispose aggregates errors; AggregateError becomes a multi-error type (Rust: a Vec in a custom error; Go: errors.Join).

ServiceSlot (handle.ts)
In JS, ServiceView/ValueView proxies give a stable facade over a mutable implementation pointer, guarded by assertAccess.
Rust: Arc<ArcSwapOption<dyn T>> (or RwLock) plus a lifecycle phase check.
Go: generic ServiceSlot[T] with atomic.Pointer and a phase check.
Error strings are asserted, for example "Facet ${id} service handles cannot be used while setting_up".

FacetKernel
- Phases: setup, assembling, connecting, activating, active, reloading, disposing, dead.
- setup must be synchronous. Rust: `fn setup(&self, env: &mut FacetEnvironment) -> Result<()>`. Go: `Setup(env *FacetEnvironment) error`. onActivate and onDeactivate register async callbacks.
- validateFacets rejects duplicate providers, mismatched modes and cycles.
- Activation uses a Kahn topological sort. Its tie-break order must match declaration order, because tests assert activation and disposal order. Facets are retired in reverse.
- own() disposables run LIFO.
- External sources come from catalogues; a source with acceptsUnavailableServices is the deferred source.
- Remote provisions go through a provider plus a loopback binding. Local singletons go into a ServiceSlot; local keyed services go into LocalKeyedServiceRegistry.
- reload is a shape-preserving replacement: validate candidates, including remote member shapes; activate them; cut over singletons via provider.replace; then retire the old facets in reverse. A failure after cutover terminates the host; a failure before cutover keeps the old generation.

combineFacetLoaders loads in order. On failure it disposes the facets already loaded in reverse and raises a multi-error. disposeLoadedFacets uses allSettled semantics.

defineService rejects an empty id and any id starting with '$chord.', and returns a frozen {id, local}. Natively this is a Service<T> token struct holding an id and a local flag.

index.ts is the public surface; it maps to lib.rs or the root chord.go re-exports. The tests rely on vi.fn spies and microtask flushing; replace them with recording closures and explicit flushes.

tasks.title: Chord facet bundle manifest, esbuild bundler, package resolver, and bundle/artifact loader
skipped_tests: packages/chord/test/bundle.test.ts (cases 'builds independent content-addressed entries and loads fresh reloadable generations', 'loads host externals through the controlled CommonJS require', and the invalid-module-export half of 'rejects corrupt entries and invalid module exports') -- these execute bundled JS via vm.compileFunction; native loaders do not run JS. Port their manifest, file naming and integrity assertions only
tasks.notes:
Formats must stay byte-compatible.

Manifest
- Constants: format "chord.facet-bundle", formatVersion 2, file name "chord-facets.json".
- Content: {format, formatVersion, plugin:{id, version?}, entries:{name:{file, integrity:"sha256-<base64>", externalImports:[sorted, deduped], sourceMap?}}}.
- Written as JSON.stringify(manifest,null,2)+"\n". Entries are sorted with localeCompare (ICU collator).

Artifact
- Format "chord.facet-bundle-artifact", version 2.
- coding-agent sends artifacts in JSON as presentationFacetBundles, so keep their fields and order the same.
- Validators reject unknown fields with exact messages.

Output file names are facet-<sha256hex(entryName)[0:12]>-[esbuild hash].cjs, with an optional .map.

Atomic output replacement
1. Build into the temp dir .<name>.tmp-<uuid>.
2. Rename any existing output to .<name>.old-<uuid>.
3. Rename the temp dir into place.
4. Remove the backup.
On Windows, a directory rename over an existing path fails, which is why the backup step exists; keep it.

esbuild options must stay identical so that hashes match:
- absWorkingDir, bundle true, format cjs, banner js '"use strict";', legalComments none
- entryNames facet-<hash12>-[hash]
- external = dedupe(['@earendil-works/chord','@earendil-works/chord/*', ...options.external])
- outExtension .js->.cjs, platform (default node)
- target: node22.19 for node, es2022 otherwise, or the user value
- supported {dynamic-import:false}, metafile true
- sourcemap 'external' or false, minify, define

Go: call github.com/evanw/esbuild/pkg/api at v0.28.2 with the same options. Map platform, target, Supported and OutExtension, and read Metafile JSON for imports with external=true.
Rust: there is no faithful crate. Spawn the esbuild 0.28.2 binary (resolve from node_modules/@esbuild/<platform>/bin/esbuild or PATH) with the equivalent CLI flags (--bundle --format=cjs --banner:js=... --entry-names=... --out-extension:.js=.cjs --supported:dynamic-import=false --metafile=...). If esbuild is unavailable, return an explicit unsupported error.
Integrity is sha256 of the file bytes, base64 encoded.

package.ts (bundleFacetPackage)
- Reads package.json name, version and peerDependencies (keys sorted) and the 'chord' config {facets, external, sourceMap}; unknown fields are rejected.
- Externals are the peers plus '<peer>/*'.
- Default entries apply only when the file exists. Configured entries override them, and false removes one.
- Path escapes are checked with realpath (Rust std::fs::canonicalize, Go filepath.EvalSymlinks + Abs).
- coding-agent passes DEFAULT_PLUGIN_FACETS {session:'src/session.ts', tui:'src/tui.ts'}.

Loaders
- readFacetBundleManifest and readFacetBundleArtifact port 1:1: validation and integrity verification.
- createFacetBundleLoader and createFacetBundleArtifactLoader cannot execute CJS natively. Port them as loaders that:
  1. validate the manifest or artifact,
  2. verify integrity,
  3. optionally materialize the artifact into a mkdtemp 'chord-facet-' directory,
  4. resolve facets from a NativeFacetRegistry keyed by (plugin.id, entryName),
  5. return an explicit error when no native facet is registered.
- Keep facetsFromModule's validation (unique ids, setup present) for registry results.
- resolveExternalTarget, validatePackageSpecifier and isBuiltin exist only for the JS require path. Keep validatePackageSpecifier for manifest validation, because externalImports must be valid specifiers.

tasks.title: Core record types, storage/session/tx contracts, document/entry/task definitions, errors, IDs, public index, package assets
skipped_tests: packages/durable/test/storage-runtime-boundary.test.ts -- scans the TS import graph for node: imports; replace with a Cargo feature / Go build-tag compile check (portable modules must build without node-env/sqlite features)
tasks.notes: types.ts defines every persisted record plus the StorageWrite union (conversation | entry | task | submission | document.create | document.copy | document.change | document.retire), CommitPublication, and the Tx/Session/Storage interfaces. Use ID newtypes: Rust #[serde(transparent)] u64 for ConversationId/EntryId/TaskId<T>/SubmissionId/DocumentId/Seq; Go named int64 types. They must serialize as bare JSON numbers. Treat all IDs as JS safe integers: max 2^53-1, and 'ID space is exhausted' is checked against Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Discriminated unions use serde tag='type'/'status'/'kind'. Field order in Rust structs and Go structs must equal the JS object-literal construction order, because records go straight into JSONL/SQLite via JSON.stringify. Optional fields are omitted, never null: skip_serializing_if / omitempty with pointer types. documents.ts details: defineDoc/defineDocFamily validate that version is a positive safe integer. resolveAddress parses overloaded arguments; in native code, use explicit enum arguments. addressId = JSON.stringify([kind, scopeKind, owner|null, key|null]) is used as an in-memory map key only. materializeDocumentValue runs migrate(value, fromVersion) and then copyJson(omitUndefinedProperties). Error classes are StorageRejected, ReadAfterWrite (message "Tx.${method}() cannot read tables after the first table write"), and ConversationBusy ("Conversation ${id} is busy"). Tests check error.name === 'StorageRejected', so expose a stable kind/name. index.ts becomes lib.rs re-exports; in Go there are no re-exports, so document the root package API instead. types.ts imports harness/types.ts and harness/types.ts imports types.ts, a type-only cycle: fine in one Rust crate; in Go both must live in the same package. types.test.ts is mostly expectTypeOf type-level assertions; port only the runtime-observable parts (serde round-trips of each variant) and drop pure type tests. docs/*.md are reference assets; spec.md (4601 lines) is the normative behavior spec for the whole area.

tasks.title: Session kernel: mutation line, Transaction staging/assembly/adopt, fork document copies, committed-state observation
tasks.notes: SessionImpl serializes all commits through one promise-chain 'mutation line'. Port it as an actor: Rust tokio task + mpsc, or a Mutex held across the async commit; Go goroutine + channel or sync.Mutex. Commit ordering and publication must be FIFO and exact. The Transaction runs these steps: (a) table reads are allowed until the first table write, after which they throw ReadAfterWrite; (b) document access goes through chord track() Trackers giving Draft proxies (beginChange/prepare/adopt/abort); (c) assemble StorageWrite[] including fork copies, checkpointWhen base-vs-delta, version migration bases, and retirements; (d) storage.commit -> Seq; (e) adopt prepared trackers (pointer swap); (f) publish to commit listeners synchronously before the commit promise resolves. Non-StorageRejected storage errors poison the session; StorageRejected aborts only that commit. The Draft proxy is the hardest part. Rust/Go need chord's native tracked-mutation API (explicit set/insert/delete ops recorded as Op), and user callbacks get a typed draft wrapper. forks.ts: an asOf copy reads the parent document at the entry's commitSeq, from the conversation the entry belongs to; a current copy reads the parent's current value; initial gets the seed. observation.ts implements the chord ReplicatedStateSource/Attachment. CommittedWatch delivers exact frames serially; with more than 100 pending (MAX_PENDING_WATCH_FRAMES) it replaces the queue with a snapshot. Retirement is published as ops [["r", null]]. Watch tests depend on microtask ordering (flush helpers). In the ports, use explicit await points / channels and deterministic test hooks rather than sleeps. ControlledStorage in session-support.ts is a storage wrapper with gating hooks; port it as a test double implementing the Storage trait/interface. Examples are runnable scripts (not vitest); port as cargo examples / Go Example tests.

tasks.title: MemoryStorage and JSONL file storage (main marker + sidecars, reclaim, recovery)
tasks.notes:
MemoryStorage behavior:
- nextId starts at 2 and seq at 1.
- Records are stored as detached deep-frozen clones (null-prototype objects; defineProperty for __proto__ keys).
- Sorted id index arrays support scans.
- prepareCommit(writes) returns {writes, apply()}; apply is idempotent and returns the same Seq.
- Documents are kept as base + delta list per document, replayed with chord applyImmutableBatches.
- Validation messages: 'ID ${id} already belongs to ${type}', 'Document address already has a current incarnation', 'version transition requires a base', 'does not retain historical content'.

Native ports clone instead of freezing. The memory-storage test asserting that mutation of a prepared write throws is JS-specific; port it as 'prepared writes are not aliased'.

JSONL on-disk format must stay byte-compatible:
- File main.jsonl holds one line per commit: {"format":1,"type":"commit","seq":N,"writes":[...]}.
- conversation, entry, submission, and document.retire writes are inline. Terminal tasks are inline as {type:'task',value}.
- Non-terminal tasks go to task-<id>.jsonl, with {type:'task.sidecar',id,ordinal} in the marker.
- document.create and document.change go to doc-<id>.jsonl as {format:1,type:'record',seq,ordinal,payload:{type:'document',id,content}}, with {type:'document.create',record,ordinal} or {type:'document.change',id,ordinal} in the marker.
- Write order: sidecars first, flushed if fsync is set, then the main marker is appended.

Reclamation runs after publish, best-effort. Current-only documents (non-conversation scope or history 'latest') are rewritten to their latest base on a base change and emptied on retire; terminal tasks' sidecars are emptied. Each rewrite writes <file>.reclaim and then renames it over the sidecar.

Recovery:
- Truncate a torn final line.
- Decode UTF-8 fatally (invalid bytes raise JsonlCorruptionError).
- Confirm each sidecar record by key JSON.stringify([file,seq,ordinal]).
- Ignore or clean stray .reclaim files and unreferenced sidecars matching /^(doc|task)-(0|[1-9]\d*)\.jsonl$/.
- After a failed write the storage is poisoned (JsonlStoragePoisonedError 'JSONL storage is poisoned and must be reopened').

All file I/O goes through the ExecutionEnv FileSystem interface (appendFile, truncateFile, flushFile, renameFile, readTextLines, openTextLineReader), so the port depends on env/index. node.ts = openNodeJsonlStorage(dir) over NodeExecutionEnv(cwd=process.cwd()). jsonl-storage.test.ts writes crafted corrupt files; JSON output must match JS byte-for-byte for those fixtures to line up.

tasks.title: Portable SQLite storage: database facade, migrations, SqliteStorage, node:sqlite adapter
tasks.notes:
The schema must be byte-identical so existing DB files open:
- durable_metadata(singleton, next_id TEXT default '2', next_seq INTEGER default 1)
- durable_schema version table, with a contiguous-version check; reject a DB newer than the code
- record_ids(id, record_type)
- conversations(id, owner_conversation_id, owner_task_id, record)
- entries(id, conversation_id, head, commit_seq, record)
- tasks(id, conversation_id, kind, status, abort_requested, background, record)
- submissions(id, conversation_id, request_id, status, record)
- documents(id, kind, family, key_value, scope_kind, owner_id, created_at, retired_at, record)
- document_revisions(document_id, seq, kind, version, content)
- all STRICT, plus the indexes in INITIAL_SCHEMA

Indexed strings (task kind, request_id, document kind, key_value) are stored as JSON.stringify(value), which keeps lone surrogates lossless. owner_id is 0 for session scope. family is 1 when key !== undefined. key_value encodes "" when there is no key. The record column is JSON.stringify(record); revision content is the JSON base value or the JSON ops array.

commit runs one transaction:
- read metadata
- checkGlobalIds (conversation/entry/document IDs unique; task/submission may be upserted but not change type)
- checkDocumentActions (StorageRejected when a copy source is changed in the same batch; live-incarnation count per address)
- table upserts
- document actions: copy materializes the source inside the tx and is wrapped in StorageRejected on failure; current-only documents delete old revisions on base or retire
- metadata update

nextId is adopted in memory only after success. document() reads inside a transaction so the record and its revisions come from one committed state. admitRead counts multi-query reads, and close waits for them to drain.

node.ts adapter:
- DatabaseSync; mkdir of the parent dir
- PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, wal_autocheckpoint (default 1000), busy_timeout 5000
- BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK; on rollback failure throw AggregateError
- SerialOperationQueue: ops run in call order and wait behind an active tx; calls made synchronously from inside the tx join it; a tx handle used after settle rejects
- statement cache per connection (prepare once)
- close runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)

Rust: rusqlite (bundled) behind a tokio Mutex or a dedicated thread, using prepare_cached. Go: database/sql + modernc.org/sqlite with SetMaxOpenConns(1), or a single *sql.Conn guarded by a mutex; explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE via Conn.ExecContext. Tests assert EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN index usage, WAL file size after checkpoint, page reuse, and bounded DB size; these are sqlite-version-sensitive, so keep the same pragmas. Integer columns: SQLite INTEGER maps to i64; JS uses number, so stay within 2^53.

tasks.notes:
env/index.ts:
- Result<T,E> = {ok:true,value} | {ok:false,error}. Map to Rust Result and Go (T, error) with typed *FileError / *ExecutionError.
- FileError codes: aborted, not_found, permission_denied, not_directory, is_directory, invalid, not_supported, unknown.
- ExecutionError codes: aborted, timeout, shell_unavailable, spawn_error, callback_error, unknown; carries an optional spillPath.
- FileSystem: about 20 async methods (absolutePath, joinPath, readTextFile, openTextLineReader, readTextLines, read/write/append/truncate/flush/rename, fileInfo, listDir, canonicalPath, exists, createDir, remove, createTempDir/File, cleanup).
- Shell.exec(command, {cwd, env, inheritEnv, timeout in seconds, onOutput, spill {afterBytes, afterLines}}).

NodeExecutionEnv (id 'node:local'):
- resolvePath expands ~ and accepts file:// URLs.
- errno codes map to FileError codes.
- Shell discovery: custom path; on Windows, Git Bash candidates then where/which; legacy WSL bash runs via stdin -s; otherwise /bin/bash, falling back to sh -c.
- Spawn detached (setsid/process group) and kill with kill(-pid, SIGKILL); on Windows use taskkill /F /T.
- Exit code = code ?? 128+signo ?? 1.
- Timeout validation (max 2147483647 ms); error message 'timeout:${timeout}'.
- After exit, wait a 100ms stdio grace, re-armed while spill is still draining.
- Spill to tmpdir/pi-output-<uuid>.log once afterBytes or afterLines is exceeded; 1 MiB high-water mark with pause/resume backpressure.
- NodeTextLineReader is strictly LF-delimited and reads 64 KiB chunks with positional reads.
- Missing cwd message: 'Working directory does not exist: ${cwd}\nCannot execute bash commands.'

Rust: tokio::process with process_group(0) + nix::sys::signal::killpg. Go: exec.Cmd with SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} + syscall.Kill(-pid); build-tagged Windows file.

truncate.ts: truncateHead never returns partial lines; byte counts are UTF-8; formatSize uses toFixed(1) with B/KB/MB.

Tools:
- Schemas are typebox Type.Object; port as literal JSON Schema with identical descriptions, since the tool declarations go to models.
- read: image sniffing (jpeg, non-animated png, gif, webp, bmp) returns an unsupported_image diagnostic; offset/limit continuation diagnostics; first-line-too-long path uses characterEnd from harness/output.
- edit: prepareArguments repairs edits sent as a JSON string, a single object, or a legacy top-level oldText/newText. Matching is exact first, then fuzzy (NFKC, trailing whitespace, smart quotes, dashes, unicode spaces) with preservation of untouched lines. BOM and CRLF are restored. details carry diff (custom numbered display) and patch (jsdiff createTwoFilesPatch with context 4, FILE_HEADERS_ONLY).
- bash: commandPrefix and prepare hooks; tail retention; full_output diagnostic.
- file-mutation-queue: a process-global map keyed `${env.id}\0${canonicalPath}`, with a canonical-parent fallback for files that do not exist yet. Rust: a static Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>; Go: a sync.Map of chans or mutexes.
- path-utils: unicode-space normalization, leading @ strip, and read fallbacks (narrow NBSP before AM/PM, NFD, curly apostrophe).

All string index math (indexOf, substring, slice in edit-diff and the fuzzy match) is UTF-16 in JS. Native code can use byte offsets internally as long as results are identical; NFKC can change lengths, and the code already handles that through line spans.

tasks.notes:
TaskScheduler is the riskiest file:
- A #live mirror of non-terminal tasks, running invocations, and a reserve/step/decide loop with precedence rules: abort marks, owner cascades, waits, completing drains.
- Task versions are migrated at reservation.
- A step that makes no durable progress (jsonEqual of before and after checkpoint) faults the task.
- Memos are first-writer-wins.
- Orphaned outcomes follow when an owner is missing.
- reconcile and finalize are scheduled via queueMicrotask.
- Waiters resolve idle/settled promises.
- Sleeps loop in chunks of MAX_TIMER_DELAY = 2^31-1 ms, cancelled with AbortSignal.any.
- Faults store {message, ...} error objects whose message text is persisted.

Rust: a single scheduler actor task owning #live, woken through a Notify; cancellation via tokio_util CancellationToken; deferred reconcile via tokio::task::yield_now or a queued self-message. Go: one goroutine with a select loop; context.Context for abort.

harness.ts:
- HarnessImpl extends SessionImpl: in Rust use composition with Deref or delegation; Go embeds *Session.
- Harness.open verifies BUILTIN_TASKS (pi.generation, pi.tool, pi.compaction) are registered, opens tasks, and closes on failure.
- root() is created lazily with agent change + init in one commit; conversation/fork creation; boundConversation.

registry.ts: createRegistry/install/uninstall/reload with snapshots and validateExtension (duplicate names, section key regex, 'instructions' reserved). define.ts holds defineTool/defineExtension/section/hook helpers. json.ts: assignJson writes leaf-by-leaf into a Draft so that ops are minimal. util.ts: Waiters, scanAll pagination, closedError.

tasks.notes:
GenerationTask:
- Phases: prepare (plan system entries and tools, threshold compaction), request (stream via Models; commit partial AssistantMessage to pi.live at most every 100ms), retry (isRetryableAssistantError/retryDelayMs; defaults enabled, maxRetries 3, baseDelay 2000, maxAgentDelay 60000), poll (deferred responses; DEFAULT_POLL_AFTER_MS 5000), tools (startToolRound spawns pi.tool children and waits; finishToolRound handles terminate/handoff/addTools).

- On context overflow it triggers overflow compaction.
- convertPartial is shared with live.ts.

ToolTask:
- Phases call/execute. Execute: readCall, prepareArguments, validateToolArguments (pi-ai), the beforeTool hook (may block or replace), run with ToolExecutionApi (output(), diagnostic(), progress details, env), the afterTool hook, finalResult, settle.
- Replay 'safe' re-runs after a crash; 'unsafe' yields an error result.
- publishProgress uses chord overlap(prev, next, 65536) to emit a front-trim + append op instead of a full rewrite (harness-live-deltas asserts the exact ops).
- appendToolResult renders diagnostics as `<harness>\n[severity] message\n</harness>`. boundContent caps text content.

output.ts:
- sanitizeOutput regex /[\x00-\x08\x0b-\x1f￹-￻]/g.
- boundOutput keeps a head/tail window on UTF-8 bytes, cutting on whole lines when possible, else on character boundaries via characterEnd/characterStart. Tests compare against Buffer behavior, including surrogate edge cases.
- OutputBuffer decodes UTF-8 split across chunks with a streaming TextDecoder.
- Progress throttles commits: the first change commits immediately, later ones wait at least 100ms and enough time for the written size at 100 KiB/s. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers, so inject a clock/timer trait (Rust) or an interface (Go) for deterministic tests.

- Phases select/summarize/retry. Default policy: reserve 16384, keepRecent 20000, background 32768.
- selectCut/isCandidate/estimateContext use pi-ai calculateContextTokens and estimateMessageTokens.
- serializeConversation truncates tool results to TOOL_RESULT_MAX_CHARS 2000 in UTF-16 code units.

All faux-provider tests port; there are no real-provider tests in vitest files.

tasks.title: ANSI/Unicode text primitives, fuzzy, word navigation, kill ring, undo stack
tasks.notes:
Every other unit builds on this one, so port it first and golden-test it heavily against TS output.

visibleWidth:
- Strips ANSI: CSI, OSC ended by BEL or ST, and APC including CURSOR_MARKER \x1b_pi:c\x07.
- Tab counts as 3 cells.
- Per-grapheme widths:
  - Zero width when every code point is Default_Ignorable, Control, Mark or Surrogate.
  - \p{RGI_Emoji} is 2.
  - A lone regional indicator is 2.
  - East Asian Wide/Fullwidth is 2, taken from the first printable code point after leading non-printing ones.
  - Spacing-mark and Thai/Lao AM special cases.
- Results go into a module-level width cache (Map).

Unicode tables:
- Generate them from the UCD version shipped with Node 22's ICU: DerivedCoreProperties, emoji-sequences and emoji-zwj-sequences for RGI_Emoji, ScriptExtensions for the CJK regex, and EastAsianWidth.
- Rust regex supports \p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}, scx= and `--` set subtraction, but not the RGI_Emoji string property.
- Go regexp supports none of these; use generated lookup tables.

JS regex semantics:
- \s and \w differ from char::is_whitespace and unicode.IsSpace (U+FEFF, U+0085). Hand-code isWhitespaceChar and PUNCTUATION_REGEX to the JS sets.

Offsets:
- Exposed offsets are UTF-16 code units: sliceWithWidth, getGraphemeCellRange, findWordBackward/findWordForward, segment indices. Provide UTF-8↔UTF-16 index helpers.

Byte-exact output:
- truncateToWidth, wrapTextWithAnsi, sliceByColumn, extractSegments, normalizeTerminalOutput, stripTerminalSequences, applyBackgroundToLine and getActiveBackgroundAnsi must match byte for byte, including where the SGR tracker re-emits state and how OSC 8 is closed.

Smaller items:
- flattenLines is a V8 rope-flattening trick; make it a no-op.
- undo-stack uses structuredClone; use Clone or a deep copy.
- fuzzy uses JS toLowerCase (full Unicode). Rust str::to_lowercase matches; Go strings.ToLower uses simple mapping (İ, final sigma), so add a special-case helper. Score index math stays in UTF-16.

word-navigation:
- Depends on Intl.Segmenter word granularity with isWordLike, which uses ICU dictionary segmentation for CJK and Thai.
- Rust: icu_segmenter WordSegmenter (auto) with word-type status.
- Go: there is no ICU equivalent. Emulate with uniseg/uax29 word boundaries plus a word-like classifier, and document the CJK/Thai divergence.

tasks.title: Color math (Oklab/OKHSL), terminal color parsing, terminal capabilities and image/hyperlink encoding
tasks.notes:
colors and oklab:
- Pure float math covering indexed/rgb/oklch/okhsl colors, parseColor, mixColors, colorToHex, 256-color quantization, foregroundAnsi/backgroundAnsi and styleText/styleTextWithAnsi.
- Keep the operation order identical.
- JS Math.round rounds half up, toward +inf; Rust f64::round and Go math.Round round half away from zero. Use floor(x+0.5).
- cbrt/pow/atan2/sin/cos can differ in the last ULP between V8 (fdlibm) and Rust std/Go math. Prefer the Rust libm crate and check results after 8-bit rounding.
- Hex output uses toString(16).padStart.

terminal-colors:
- Parses OSC 10/11/4 replies of the form rgb:R/G/B with 1-4 hex digits per channel, scaled to 8 bits, ended by BEL or ST.
- Parses the color-scheme DSR `CSI ?997;1|2n`.

terminal-image, capability detection:
- Reads env at call time: TERM_PROGRAM, TERM, TERMINAL_EMULATOR, COLORTERM, KITTY_WINDOW_ID, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, WEZTERM_PANE, WARP_*, ITERM_SESSION_ID, WT_SESSION.
- With TMUX set, it runs a synchronous probe: execSync `tmux display-message -p '#{client_termfeatures}'`.
- Overrides: PI_HYPERLINKS, PI_IMAGE_PROTOCOL, PI_TRUE_COLOR.
- Capabilities are cached in module globals with set/reset/override hooks used by tests and coding-agent.
- Rust: OnceLock/Mutex. Go: sync.Mutex package vars.
- Inject the env reader and the tmux probe so tests can control them.

terminal-image, encoders:
- Kitty: a=T,f=100,q=2, base64 chunks of 4096 chars with m=1/0, C=1 when moveCursor is false, i=/p= ids, delete d=I/A/a, placement and crop parsing via a module-global metadata registry, and a global image id counter.
- iTerm2: OSC 1337 with size computed by Buffer.byteLength(b64,'base64'), which is a formula and not a decode, and name=base64(utf8).

terminal-image, dimensions and links:
- PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP dimension parsers decode with Buffer.from(b64,'base64'), which is lenient: it skips invalid chars, accepts url-safe chars and tolerates missing padding. Implement a lenient decoder in both languages; the standard decoders are strict.
- hyperlink() emits `\x1b]8;;URL\x07text\x1b]8;;\x07`.
- imageFallback shortens the home dir to ~ and uses pathToFileURL. Replicate Node's percent-encoding exactly; url::Url::from_file_path and net/url differ.
- isImageLine uses includes() of the Kitty and iTerm2 prefixes.

tasks.title: Key sequence parsing, stdin sequence buffering, keybinding registry

tasks.notes:
keys.ts:
- Parses:
  - Kitty CSI-u: codepoint:shifted:base ; mods:event-type ; text-codepoints, including release (:3) and repeat (:2).
  - xterm modifyOtherKeys: CSI 27;mod;code~.

stdin-buffer.ts:
- EventEmitter with 'data' and 'paste' events; map to callbacks or channels.
- A completeness state machine for CSI, OSC, DCS, APC, SS3, SGR mouse and X10 mouse.
- Timeouts: 10ms for a lone ESC, 50ms for other partial sequences, configurable.
- Accumulates bracketed paste, fixes WezTerm's `ESC ESC [`, and dedups Kitty printables.

tasks.notes:
Terminal interface (tests and coding-agent implement it):
- start(onInput, onResize), stop, drainInput(maxMs, idleMs), write, columns/rows, kittyProtocolActive, moveBy.
- hide/showCursor, clearLine/clearFromCursor/clearScreen, setTitle (OSC 0), setProgress (OSC 9;4 plus a keepalive timer).

ProcessTerminal:
- Raw mode. Rust: crossterm or rustix termios. Go: golang.org/x/term.
- Resize. Rust: signal-hook. Go: os/signal, plus the Windows console path.
- refreshTerminalDimensions sends SIGWINCH to itself. Ignore EACCES/EPERM and skip on win32.
- Dimension fallback reads COLUMNS/LINES.
- Kitty negotiation:
  - Writes `\x1b[>7u\x1b[?u\x1b[c` and parses replies via parseKeyboardProtocolNegotiationSequence, with a 150ms fragment timeout.
  - Falls back to modifyOtherKeys `\x1b[>4;2m`.
  - Teardown writes `\x1b[<u` / `\x1b[>4;0m` and `\x1b[?2004l`.
- normalizeAppleTerminalInput and normalizeNativeShiftEnterInput use isNativeModifierPressed('shift').
- Env: PI_TUI_ESC_TIMEOUT (resolveEscapeTimeoutMs), PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG (append every write to a file), TERM_PROGRAM, SSH_*.
- Node TTY writes are synchronous, so use blocking writes.
- drainInput discards pending stdin before exit.

Native helpers:
- Replace createRequire .node loading with compiled-in code exposing get_text, get_image (PNG/BMP bytes), get_file_paths (darwin), set_text (darwin/win32), is_modifier_pressed(shift|command|control|option) and enable_virtual_terminal_input (win32).
- Keep the tri-state results: None = unavailable, Some(None) = empty, Err = failure.
- Linux:
  - Available only when DISPLAY is set, rechecked on every call; Wayland without DISPLAY → none.
  - Reads via XCB with a 2s deadline, INCR support, a 50MB cap and the same target preference lists.
  - Runs on a private worker thread with a 3s wait; it stays unavailable while a read is stalled.
- Darwin:
  - NSPasteboard string, PNG, or TIFF converted to PNG; file URLs become POSIX paths.
  - Modifiers from CGEventSourceFlagsState.
- Win32:
  - GetAsyncKeyState and SetConsoleMode VT input.
  - CF_UNICODETEXT read/write with OpenClipboard retries.
  - Images from the PNG format, or CF_DIBV5/CF_DIB converted to a BMP file.
- Rust crates: objc2/objc2-app-kit/core-graphics, windows-sys, x11rb (or libloading of libxcb.so.1 to keep the runtime-optional dependency).
- Go packages: cgo or ebitengine/purego for AppKit, golang.org/x/sys/windows, jezek/xgb.
- Run clipboard calls on a blocking thread or goroutine.
- The .node prebuilds, napi.h, clipboard.h and build scripts are reference only; the ports do not ship them.

Tests:
- native-platform.test.ts: port only the DISPLAY/WAYLAND lazy-availability and helper-identity semantics, using a fake backend.
- Drop the ELF 64KB-page prebuild check. Keep the Windows clipboard write test env-gated (PI_TEST_NATIVE_CLIPBOARD=1).
- Port the env/platform-mutating tests behind injectable env and platform providers.

packages/tui/test/viewport-overwrite-repro.ts -- manual repro script for a real terminal, not an automated test
tasks.notes:
Component model (tui.ts):
- Component trait: render(width)->Vec<String>, optional handle_input, handle_mouse → {handled, render, focus}, wants_key_release, invalidate, and the Focusable focused flag. Optional JS methods become trait default methods (Rust) or optional interfaces checked by type assertion (Go).
- Identity: focus, overlays and removeChild compare with ===. Use Rc::ptr_eq in Rust and pointer equality in Go.
- Symbol.for brands: VIEWPORT_TUI and LAYOUT_NODE become trait methods returning an Option.
- Container, dispatchMouseEvent/retargetMouseEvent.

Overlays:
- OverlayOptions: width/minWidth/maxHeight as a number or 'N%', 9 anchors, offsets, absolute or percent row/col, margin, visible(w,h), nonCapturing.
- OverlayHandle and a focus-restore state machine.
- compositeOverlays/compositeTuiLine splice overlay text by column with SEGMENT_RESET `\x1b[0m\x1b]8;;\x07` and applyLineResets, and must not split CJK wide chars.
- extractCursorPosition handles CURSOR_MARKER for the hardware cursor.

Input pipeline (handleTerminalInput):
- Swallows cell-size replies `\x1b[6;h;wt` (after a `\x1b[16t` query), OSC 10/11/4 replies ended by the DA1 sentinel (queryTerminalColors), color-scheme `?997` reports (after `\x1b[?2031h`) and focus in/out.
- Then key-release filtering, input listeners, the debug key, and routing to the focused overlay or component.

Render scheduling:
- requestRender coalesces via process.nextTick, then throttles to 16ms using performance.now and setTimeout. requestRender(true) forces a full redraw.
- Implement this on a single-threaded UI loop with an injectable clock. Tests await nextTick+20ms (waitForRender), which maps to running pending tasks and advancing the clock.

tui-main-screen.ts:
- Differential renderer over previousLines: finds the first and last changed lines, moves the cursor relatively, wraps output in synchronized output `\x1b[?2026h/l`, and redraws fully on width change or changes above the viewport (TERMUX_VERSION special case).
- A line wider than the terminal writes a crash log (pi-tui-crash.log) and throws.
- Debug logs: PI_TUI_DEBUG and PI_TUI_DEBUG_REDRAW, written to /tmp/tui/render-*.log.
- Parses Kitty image ids from removed lines and deletes the images.
- BoundedTerminalWriter writes 1MiB chunks without splitting surrogate pairs; in Rust/Go, split on char boundaries.
- captureRenderState/restoreRenderState are used by coding-agent.

image.ts:
- Kitty: the sequence on the first line, then rows-1 empty lines.
- iTerm2: rows-1 empty lines, then `CSI nA` plus the sequence.
- Allocates ids from the global counter.

Tests:
- virtual-terminal.ts wraps @xterm/headless. Port it on a VT emulator: Rust alacritty_terminal or vt100; Go charmbracelet/x/vt or vt10x.
- Viewport lines are right-trimmed (translateToString(true)). Wide-char and pending-wrap behavior must match xterm.js closely.

tasks.title: Alt-screen layout engine, stacks, ScrollView, and simple components (Box, Text, TruncatedText, Spacer, Loader, CancellableLoader, MouseRegion)
tasks.notes:
layout.ts:
- renderLayoutFrame/layoutComponent walk LAYOUT_NODE trees (vstack/hstack/scroll) to compute rects, then paint into a frame of strings via compositeTuiLine.
- Preserves OSC 133 prompt zone prefixes.
- Crops Kitty images partially scrolled out (cropKittyImageLine/getKittyImageMetadata).
- Scrollbar track/thumb geometry and painting.
- Hit-tests mouse events to component-local coordinates.

stack.ts:
- allocateStackSizes: basis/grow/shrink/min/max, plus a distribution loop with Math.floor weights and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER sentinels. Use i64 and avoid usize overflow in capacity math.
- visibleStackEntries applies the visible(viewport) predicates.
- HStack measures intrinsic width by rendering at full width, then renders again at the allocated width.

ScrollView:
- Exactly one child; addChild, removeChild and clear throw.
- follow 'end', primary, overscroll chain/contain.
- scrollbar hidden/auto/always. The auto hide timer defaults to 1000ms and is unref'd: it must not keep the process alive and must fire on the UI thread.
- scrollTo/scrollBy/scrollToStart/scrollToEnd/updateLayout clamp rules and followSuppressedAtEnd are covered by layout.test.ts.

Other components:
- Box cache: compares child lines by string identity (cheap in V8). Compare content, or use Rc<str> ptr_eq as a fast path. It detects bgFn changes by sampling bgFn('test'). It also keeps the mouse layout.
- Text/TruncatedText: tabs become 3 spaces, padding is clamped, applyBackgroundToLine.
- Loader: setInterval at 80ms over braille frames and prepends an empty line.
- CancellableLoader: AbortController becomes a CancellationToken (Rust) or context.CancelFunc (Go).
- MouseRegion.

Output must be byte-identical, including space padding to width. truncated-text.test.ts uses chalk; replace it with a tiny SGR helper that mimics chalk level 3.

tasks.title: Input, SelectList, SettingsList components, autocomplete providers, EditorComponent interface
tasks.notes:
Input:
- Buffers its own bracketed paste: strips newlines, tabs become 4 spaces.
- Keybinding-driven editing, kill ring with accumulate/prepend, undo coalescing ('type-word').
- Grapheme-aware cursor stored as a UTF-16 offset.
- Horizontal scroll via sliceByColumn.
- Draws a fake cursor `\x1b[7m..\x1b[27m` and emits CURSOR_MARKER when focused; placeholder rendering.
- Mouse click positions the cursor.

SelectList:
- Filters by lowercase value prefix and keeps a centered visible window.
- Renders '→ ' and two-column layout with descriptions when width > 40 (default primary column 32), a truncatePrimary hook, '  (i/n)' scroll info and 'No matching commands'.
- Wheel scrolling, and press/click select semantics.

SettingsList:
- Optional search Input using fuzzyFilter on label, value cycling and description wrap.
- Submenu factory returns a Component and receives a done(value?, {navigateTo}) closure. This needs a Weak/RefCell back-reference in Rust and a closure over a pointer in Go.

autocomplete.ts:
- AutocompleteProvider trait: async getSuggestions(lines, line, col, {signal, force}), applyCompletion, optional shouldTriggerFileCompletion and triggerCharacters.
- CombinedAutocompleteProvider:
  - Slash commands with async argument completions.
  - '@' fuzzy file search by spawning `fd` with the same args (base dir, --type, --hidden, --exclude .git patterns, --max-depth, --full-path when the query has '/', a query built by buildFdPathQuery). SIGKILL on abort; .git results are filtered.
  - readdir path completion with ~ expansion (homedir), quoted paths with spaces, Windows separator display normalization, and a '/' suffix for directories.
  - Scoring, then sort with localeCompare (ICU root collation). Rust: icu_collator. Go: x/text/collate. Sorts must be stable; in Go use sort.SliceStable.
- Cursor columns and prefix lengths are UTF-16 offsets.

editor-component.ts:
- The EditorComponent interface coding-agent uses for custom editors. Make it a trait/interface; native implementations only, no TS loading.

Tests:
- autocomplete.test.ts gates its fd cases on fd being installed, and uses temp dirs and symlinks.

tasks.title: Multi-line Editor component
skipped_tests: packages/tui/test/chat-simple.ts -- interactive demo app using ProcessTerminal and chalk, not a test
tasks.notes:
Text state and wrapping:
- State: lines, cursorLine, and cursorCol as a UTF-16 offset.
- Sticky-column state: preferredVisualCol and snappedFromCursorCol, following the documented decision table.
- scrollOffset and lastWidth.
- buildVisualLineMap uses wordWrapLine, which is exported and tested directly and returns {text, startIndex, endIndex}.

Paste markers:
- Pastes over 10 lines or over 1000 UTF-16 chars become '[paste #N +L lines]' or '[paste #N C chars]'.
- segmentWithMarkers merges Intl.Segmenter output so markers are atomic for cursor movement, deletion and wrapping.
- Deleting a marker renumbers the higher ids and their registry entries.
- expandPasteMarkers runs on submit, and the result is trimmed.

handlePaste:
- Decodes CSI-u ctrl sequences (`ESC[n;5u`), normalizes CRLF and tabs, and drops control chars except \n.
- Prefixes a space before a path-like paste that follows a word char.

Editing features:
- History browse with a draft (structuredClone).
- Kill ring (accumulate/prepend), yank/yank-pop, undo snapshots that deep-copy the lines and the pastes map.
- Jump-to-char forward/backward.
- Page scroll moves max(5, 30% of rows) lines.
- Backslash+Enter inserts a newline when submit is bound to shift+enter; disableSubmit.

Autocomplete:
- Trigger and debounce regexes are built from the trigger chars (default '@' plus provider chars).
- Slash-command context only on the first line.
- Attachment queries are debounced.
- An async request chain uses startToken, requestId, AbortController and a text/cursor snapshot check before applying results.
- Tab auto-applies a forced query that returns exactly one result; best-match selection.
- Rust: run provider futures on the UI LocalSet or send results back over a channel. Go: run them in goroutines and post results to the UI loop. Keep the stale-result rejection exact.

Render:
- Border lines with '↑/↓ N more' indicators, padding, fake cursor plus CURSOR_MARKER, and a SelectList appended below.
- handleMouse positions the cursor.

Tests:
- editor.test.ts (4.4k lines) is the main parity suite. It uses TuiMainScreen, VirtualTerminal and a CombinedAutocompleteProvider over temp dirs.
- test-themes.ts uses chalk level 3; port it to a helper that emits chalk's exact SGR open/close codes, including chalk's nested re-open behavior.

tasks.title: Alternate-screen TUI (TuiAltScreen), alt-screen search, wheel acceleration, flash messages

packages/tui/test/render-churn-bench.ts -- benchmark using the node:inspector profiler, not a test

TuiAltScreen (ViewportTUI) setup and rendering:
- Enters the alternate screen `?1049h` and enables SGR mouse (1006 plus button/any-motion modes), focus events and color-scheme notifications.
- Paints a full frame with renderLayoutFrame, diffs it per row and rewrites changed rows with absolute CUP inside synchronized output.

Selection and copy:

- Word selection uses Intl.Segmenter word isWordLike plus joiners, with the same CJK caveat as word-navigation.

tasks.title: LaTeX math to Unicode renderer
tasks.notes:
API: renderLatex(source, {display}) returns Option<String>, which is None for unsupported or malformed input.

Parser:
- Recursive-descent LatexParser over JS string positions (source[i], slice, indexOf), i.e. UTF-16 units.
- Iterate by code point in Rust/Go, but replicate the Array.from (code point) length checks used by formatScript, formatFraction, accents, \not and mathbb.

Markers:
- Uses supplementary Private Use Area markers U+F0000–F0005 for layout nodes, named operators and protected spaces.
- NEGATIVE_SPACE is \u0000.

Regexes:
- Some use lookbehind/lookahead with \p{L}\p{N} and the u flag (named-operator spacing), and LAYOUT_MARKER_PATTERN uses /gu.
- Rust's regex crate has no lookaround and Go's regexp has none; write manual scanners or use fancy-regex/regexp2.
- JS trim/trimStart/trimEnd and /\s/ use the JS whitespace set (including U+FEFF, U+00A0 and line terminators). Implement a js_trim helper.

2D layout:
- Stacked fractions with '─'.
- Operator limits for sum, int, lim and operatorname*.
- Sub/superscript stacking in display mode.
- Matrices: pmatrix/bmatrix/Bmatrix/vmatrix/Vmatrix delimiters and ' │ ' column joins.
- Cases with ⎧⎨⎩.
- joinLayouts uses baseline alignment, padLayoutLine centers with Math.floor, and the final pass removes common indentation.

Copy SYMBOLS, NEGATED_SYMBOLS, BLACKBOARD, SUPERSCRIPTS, SUBSCRIPTS, ACCENTS and the command sets verbatim. latex.test.ts is the golden suite and imports renderLatex via the index.

tasks.title: Markdown component (marked lexer port + ANSI renderer) and public API barrel/package metadata
tasks.notes:
Marked lexer:
- markdown.ts needs a faithful port of the marked 18.0.11 Lexer, Tokenizer and rules (GFM: tables, task lists, autolinks/url, html block/inline, escapes, br, space tokens, loose lists, list item raw/text) plus marked's extension mechanism (start() index hints and custom tokenizers).
- This repo uses that mechanism for latexBlock/latex tokens, and replaces del with STRICT_STRIKETHROUGH_REGEX via a Tokenizer subclass.
- pulldown-cmark, comrak and goldmark produce different trees (no 'space' tokens, different raw/text, html splitting, list looseness), which would break markdown.test.ts goldens.
- Budget about 2-3k extra lines for a hand-ported marked module.
- Export Marked/Token/Tokens equivalents, because coding-agent mermaid.ts calls new Marked().lexer().
- marked's regexes use lookaround: use fancy-regex or hand scanners in Rust, and dlclark/regexp2 (ECMAScript mode) or hand scanners in Go.

LaTeX tokenizers:
- tokenizeInlineLatex/tokenizeBlockLatex cover $, $$, \( and \[, plus heuristics for pending (streaming) math.

Renderer:
- Tabs become 3 spaces.
- trimPartialClosingFences handles streaming (issue #5825).
- Headings: h1 is bold+underline; '### ' prefix only for depth ≥3.
- Style-prefix sentinel trick: call the style fn on '\u0000' and keep the prefix, to re-apply styles after inner resets.
- Blockquote uses a '│ ' border and re-applies quote style after `\x1b[0m`.
- Lists:
  - Markers are '- ' or 'N. ', with preserveOrderedListMarkers and task '[x] '.
  - Nesting indent is 4 spaces.
- Tables:
  - Proportional width allocation with floor plus leftover distribution, and a raw-markdown fallback when too narrow.
  - Cell wrap reset `\x1b[22;23;24;25;27;28;29;39m`.
- Code blocks use highlightCode and codeBlockIndent.
- hr is min(width, 80).
- Links are OSC 8 when capabilities.hyperlinks; otherwise a ' (url)' suffix with mailto: stripped.
- LaTeX goes through renderLatex unless pending or renderLatex is false.
- Output is cached by (text, width). The WeakRef token cache becomes a plain cache.

Public API and tests:
- index.ts is the public API barrel: lib.rs pub use in Rust, package exports in Go.
- package.json, README, CHANGELOG and tsconfig are metadata only.
- markdown.test.ts uses chalk, VirtualTerminal and TuiMainScreen.

tasks.title: MCP client core: JSON-RPC protocol, content conversion, McpClient, in-memory and stdio transports, package scaffolding
tasks.notes:
Crate/module scaffolding:
- package.json exports ".", "./oauth" and "./testing". Map them to a Rust crate pi-mcp with pub mods oauth and testing, and a Go module with packages mcp, mcp/oauth and mcp/mcptest.
- The facade src/index.ts lives in unit mcp-http-oauth because it re-exports StreamableHttpTransport. Tests in this unit import modules directly.

McpClient (client.ts):
- Numeric request ids from 1. Pending map keyed by id.
- LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION="2025-11-25". Supported versions: 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05. An unsupported negotiated version is a connect error.
- Sends notifications/initialized after initialize.
- When onProgress is set, progressToken = request id. Timeout default 30000ms, reset on progress when resetTimeoutOnProgress; Infinity or <=0 disables it.
- Abort sends notifications/cancelled {requestId, reason?}, never for initialize.
- Pagination is capped at MAX_LIST_PAGES=1000 and rejects a repeated cursor; nextCursor "" or null ends it.
- A missing resource name falls back to the uri. A missing CallToolResult.content becomes [].
- Built-in request handlers: ping and roots/list (roots from options).
- Incoming requests are handled fire-and-forget (no ordering guarantee between concurrent handlers). Unknown methods answer -32601.
- Error classes and exact messages: McpError(code,message,data), McpConnectionClosedError "MCP connection closed", McpTimeoutError "MCP request timed out after ${ms}ms", McpAbortError (name AbortError).

toLlmContent (protocol/content.ts):
- Exact placeholder strings: `[audio <mime> omitted]`, resource_link -> `name: uri`, `[binary resource uri (type) omitted]`, `[unsupported MCP content <type>]`.
- structuredContent is rendered as JSON.stringify(v,null,2). Needs key-order-preserving JSON (serde_json preserve_order; ordered map in Go) and JS number formatting.

InMemoryTransport:
- Delivers via structuredClone + queueMicrotask, so send() resolves before the peer sees the message.
- Native: unbounded channel plus a spawned delivery task, deep-copying the JSON value.

StdioTransport:
- Spawned through cross-spawn: resolve PATHEXT and .cmd/.bat shims on Windows; Rust uses the `which` crate plus hand-ported cmd escaping, Go uses exec.LookPath.
- Env is merged with process.env.
- Newline-delimited JSON; lines over DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (16MiB) error out. stderr is kept in a 64KiB ring buffer and included in close and exit errors.
- Process groups: detached + kill(-pid). Rust: CommandExt::process_group(0) + libc::kill(-pid). Go: SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} + syscall.Kill(-pid). On win32: `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`.
- Close sequence: end stdin, wait a 500ms grace period, SIGTERM the group, then SIGKILL after grace + closeTimeoutMs (2000). Keep this timing.
- A process-exit hook kills live groups. Native: a global registry drained from the exit path and signal handlers.

Tests:
- client.test.ts uses vi.useFakeTimers. Use tokio::time::pause in Rust and an injectable clock or short real timeouts in Go.
- stdio fixtures are Node .mjs scripts. Rewrite them as native helper programs (Rust: a test bin via CARGO_BIN_EXE_*; Go: TestMain re-exec of os.Args[0] keyed by an env var) with identical JSON replies. The stubborn-server test stays POSIX-only.
- coding-agent/test/mcp-command.test.ts also reuses stdio-server.mjs; expose the native fixture so that unit can use it.

tasks.title: MCP streamable HTTP transport with SSE, OAuth 2.1 auth flow, callback server, and package facade
tasks.notes:
StreamableHttpTransport requests:
- POST with `accept: application/json, text/event-stream` and content-type application/json.
- A JSON response body may be a single message or an array.
- 202/204 to a request (as opposed to a notification) is an error.
- Session header Mcp-Session-Id. After initialize, MCP-Protocol-Version is sent.
- close() sends DELETE with a 1s timeout. 404 on a request that carried a session -> McpSessionExpiredError. Other failures -> McpHttpError(status, body).

GET stream:
- Opened after notifications/initialized. 405 means the server offers none.
- Reconnect delay 1000*2^n ms capped at 30000, maxRetries 5. A server `retry:` field overrides the delay. Resume with Last-Event-ID.
- Retryable: status 408, 429, >=500, network errors (TypeError), error codes starting E* or UND_ERR*. Native code needs a typed network-error kind.

consumeSseStream (exported, tested directly):
- Handles CRLF/CR/LF, BOM and comments.
- An `id` containing NUL is ignored. `retry` must be all digits.
- Byte limits are counted in UTF-8 bytes. Event fields: event/data/id/retry.

Auth:
- On 401, or 403 whose WWW-Authenticate matches /(?:^|[\s,])error="?insufficient_scope"?/i, call authProvider.onUnauthorized({response, serverUrl, fetch, token}) once and retry; a second failure raises McpAuthRequiredError.
- The Cloudflare `fetch` receiver fix (#10188) is JS-only and does not apply natively.

OAuth discovery (port of MCP TS SDK 1.29, keep LICENSES text and attribution):
- Protected resource: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource{path}, then the root.
- Authorization server: oauth-authorization-server{path}, openid-configuration{path}, {path}/.well-known/openid-configuration.
- 4xx and 502 count as a miss. Send the MCP-Protocol-Version header.
- Issuer comparison ignores a trailing slash (OAuthIssuerMismatchError).

OAuth flow:
- PKCE: verifier = base64url(32 random bytes), challenge S256. DCR via POST registration_endpoint (default /register).
- Token requests are application/x-www-form-urlencoded (URLSearchParams: space as +). Client auth: client_secret_basic (Basic base64(urlencode(id):urlencode(secret))), client_secret_post or none, chosen from token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.
- Check RFC 9207 `iss` on the callback.
- Retries: invalid_client/unauthorized_client clear all state and rerun; invalid_grant clears tokens and reruns.
- stepUpScope merges granted and challenged scopes.
- adaptOAuthProvider shares a single in-flight refresh. McpOAuthProvider serializes its writes and binds state to the exact server URL string.
- Use WHATWG URL semantics (Rust `url` crate; Go needs careful net/url handling of path, trailing slash and origin).

OAuthCallbackServer:
- HTTP on 127.0.0.1, port 0 or configured. IPv6 hosts are bracketed in redirect URIs.
- 5 minute timeout. Success/error HTML pages are supplied by the caller.
- Rust: hyper 1.x server on tokio. Go: net/http.

Tests:
- helpers.ts starts a loopback node:http server; rewrite as a native loopback server helper.
- oauth.test covers discovery, registration, PKCE, refresh, concurrent 401s, step-up, URL binding, issuer mismatch, the configured metadata URL, the iss check and the callback pages.

tasks.title: Codemode package: source options parsing, TypeScript declaration rendering, QuickJS-WASM sandbox host/worker and prelude
tasks.notes:
This is the largest hidden porting cost. quickjs-wasi's JS glue (node_modules/quickjs-wasi/dist/index.js ~3100 lines, plus wasi-shim.js) must be reimplemented natively against node_modules/quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm (v3.6.2). Vendor the .wasm into both repos, using include_bytes! in Rust and go:embed in Go.

WASM exports used:
- Setup and limits: _initialize, qjs_init, qjs_set_memory_limit, qjs_set_max_stack_size (MAX_STACK_SIZE=512*1024), qjs_set_interrupt_handler.
- Eval and calls: qjs_eval(code,len,filename,flags), qjs_call, qjs_new_host_function(namePtr,nameLen,id).
- Values: qjs_new_string, qjs_new_number, qjs_get_undefined/true/false/global, qjs_get_prop_value, qjs_set_prop_string, qjs_dup_value, qjs_free_value.
- Exceptions: qjs_is_exception, qjs_get_exception, qjs_throw, qjs_new_error.
- Jobs: qjs_is_job_pending, qjs_execute_pending_job.
- Strings: qjs_get_string_len (length-aware WTF-8) + qjs_free_cstring. Type checks: qjs_is_undefined, qjs_is_string.
- Memory: wasm_malloc, wasm_free.

env imports:
- host_call(namePtr,nameLen,thisPtr,argc,argvPtr): returns a dup'd value, or 0 after qjs_throw.
- host_interrupt: polls the atomic abort flag.
- host_promise_rejection: frees values.
- host_module_normalize/load: unused, return an error.
- host_get_timezone_offset.

wasi_snapshot_preview1 shim:
- clock_time_get returns Date.now()*1e6 for both clocks.
- fd_write discards output but reports full length.
- fd_fdstat_get reports a char device for fds 1/2. fd_close/fd_seek return NOSYS(52).
- random_get, args/environ empty, proc_exit.
- Values cross the boundary as WTF-8. Lone surrogates cannot live in a Rust String or valid Go UTF-8, so decode lossily at the boundary or keep the WTF-8 bytes.

Host/worker (runtime/host.ts, worker.ts):
- The Node worker plus SharedArrayBuffer becomes a dedicated OS thread (Rust) or goroutine (Go) owning the wasm Store, fed by a channel carrying the protocol.ts message kinds (start/result/abort; bridge kinds call/global/output/done).
- Interrupt: an AtomicBool polled by host_interrupt. Backstops: wasmtime epoch_interruption, wazero WithCloseOnContextDone. Cap linear memory with wasmtime StoreLimits / wazero WithMemoryLimitPages.
- Embed PRELUDE_SOURCE verbatim and eval it with filename "codemode-prelude.js". Call it with a JSON string of the globals.
- Wrap the script exactly as `(async (tools, console) => {${code}\n})` with filename "codemode.js".
- drain(): loop executePendingJobs, then call api.stalled(). Settle tool results via api.settle.
- Result error kinds: script, timeout, aborted, sandbox. DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000.
- Prelude store limits: MAX_STORE_VALUE_CHARS 262144, MAX_STORE_TOTAL_CHARS 1048576. These are UTF-16 lengths computed inside the VM, so no native concern.
- RESERVED_GLOBALS and the global-name validation error strings must match.
- The "Worker exited with code" message is Node-specific; map it to a sandbox error with similar text.

wasm.ts:
- loadQuickJSWasm caches compiled modules per path. Native: compile the embedded bytes once (wasmtime Module / wazero CompiledModule plus compilation cache). Keep an optional override path for parity with config getQuickJSWasmPath.

declarations.ts:
- Emits TypeScript text for the model; it must be byte-identical.
- MCP_TYPESCRIPT_PREAMBLE verbatim. schemaToType sorts keys (JS default sort = UTF-16 code unit order) and resolves local $ref with MAX_REF_EXPANSIONS 32. DEFAULT_INPUT_SCHEMA_MAX_CHARS 16000 is measured in UTF-16 units.
- Also renderToolSignature/renderToolSample/renderToolOutputType/mcpStructuredContentSchema.

source.ts:
- parseCodemodeSource reads an optional first line `// @options: {...}` with keys max_output_tokens and timeout_ms (positive integers <= 2147483647).
- CodemodeSourceError messages embed V8 JSON.parse messages that cannot be reproduced; adapt the test assertions to the native message where they compare it.
- Keep CODEMODE_SOURCE_GRAMMAR (Lark) verbatim.

identifier.ts:
- toCodemodeIdentifier works per code point: ASCII [A-Za-z_$] first, [A-Za-z0-9_$] rest, otherwise '_'. "" becomes "_".

sandbox.test.ts adjustments:
- Skip the cases "accepts a worker path string" and "reports a missing worker file as a sandbox error" (Node worker file URL option; drop workerUrl from the native API).
- Replace the node:vm parse check "embedded sources parse as JavaScript" with a QuickJS compile-only eval.
- Adapt "reports a failing wasm module" to invalid wasm bytes.

tasks.title: Built-in codemode extension (tool, executor, renderer) and tool_search extension (BM25)
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/codemode-worker-config.test.ts -- tests config.ts resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier for Bun/bundled/unbundled JS worker entrypoints; native runs the embedded wasm in-process, no worker specifier
tasks.notes:
Extension registration (codemode/index.ts):
- createCodemodeExtension registers CODEMODE_TOOL_NAME="codemode" with defaultActive false. Mode comes from settings.codemode.mode; inlineBudget is read from settings.
- This is a native ExtensionFactory implementation of the ExtensionAPI trait/interface.

Tool definition (tool.ts):
- Schema `{code: string}` with description "Raw JavaScript source.".
- isCodemodeTool and isToolSearchTool compare schema object identity. Natively, compare a tool marker or kind id, never the name, because other extensions' tools named codemode/tool_search must not match.
- Description: DESCRIPTION_INTRO + describeGlobals + a catalog.
  - Budget DEFAULT_CODEMODE_INLINE_BUDGET=3000 tokens at CHARS_PER_TOKEN 4.
  - selectCatalog fills round-robin, cheapest first, and says what is missing.
  - Namespaces are sorted with localeCompare.
  - Deferred tools and namespace instructions are left out.
- prepareCodemodeLoadout implements modes on/only. constrainedSampling = {grammar openai_lark: CODEMODE_SOURCE_GRAMMAR}. exposure "model-only".

Execution (execute.ts):
- Nested calls go through ctx.executeTool with ids `${toolCallId}/...`, so hooks and permissions apply. Calls run in parallel.
- Memory limit 256MiB. Timeout defaults to Infinity unless timeout_ms is given.
- Store: CODEMODE_STORE_ENTRY_TYPE "codemode-store" custom entries. readCodemodeStore folds them from the root along the current branch and ignores malformed data. Append nothing for failed scripts or scripts without writes.
- Output budget: DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 10000 (x4 chars, UTF-16 lengths), head/tail split. The full text spills to os.tmpdir()/pi-codemode-<16 hex>.txt.
- Result header: "Script completed|failed\nWall time X.X seconds\nOutput:\n" (toFixed(1)).
- Discovery globals searchTools/describeTool/describeNamespace use tool-search Bm25Ranker.
- models globals:
  - getModelsOfType, getAvailableOfType, getModelOfType, classify, generateImages, with a concurrency limiter of 4.
  - Classifier and images contexts are validated. Headers are stripped from model info, and script-supplied auth fields are ignored.
- Usage of nested results is summed via usage-totals.

Renderer (renderer.ts):
- SCRIPT_HEADER regex; CODE_PREVIEW_LINES 10, CALL_PREVIEW_COUNT 8, OUTPUT_PREVIEW_LINES 5; icons ✓ ✗ ⊘ ….
- formatCost: toFixed(2) at >=0.01, else toPrecision(2). Port JS toPrecision exactly.
- Collapsed output is limited by wrapped visual lines.

Lazy loading:
- execute.lazy.ts (dynamic import) becomes a direct call.
- codemode/worker.ts is the bundle-only worker entry; drop it natively (it only re-exports pi-codemode/worker).

tool-search (tool.ts):
- STOP_WORDS set, naive stem (plural folding), tokenize (camelCase/snake_case split, lowercase).
- createToolSearchDocument concatenates name, description, namespace and schemaText.
