tasks.title: Session JSONL persistence, tree, projection, listing; LLM message conversion; branch export
tasks.notes:
Byte-compatible on-disk format.
- CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION=3. Header {type:"session",version,id,timestamp,cwd,parentSession?}.
- Entry types: message, thinking_level_change, model_change, usage, compaction, branch_summary, custom, custom_message, context_edit, label, session_info.
- Key order differs per entry type: custom puts {type,customType,data,id,parentId,timestamp}; most others start with {type,id,parentId,timestamp}. Mirror the TS object-literal order exactly.
- JSON.stringify drops undefined fields.
- Messages must round-trip verbatim, including unknown provider fields. Use serde_json preserve_order or a Value-backed message in Rust, and json.RawMessage or an ordered map in Go.
- Number output must follow the JS Number.prototype.toString algorithm.

Ids and file naming.
- Entry id = randomUUID().slice(0,8), checked for collisions against byId; falls back to a full UUID.
- Session id = uuidv7 from the pi-ai port.
- Dir name: `--${cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/,'').replace(/[/\\:]/g,'-')}--` under agentDir/sessions.
- File name: `${iso.replace(/[:.]/g,'-')}_${id}.jsonl`.

Persistence.
- Lazy flush: nothing is written until the first assistant message (#10000).
- First flush opens with the `wx` flag and writes all entries; later entries use appendFileSync.
- Fork/import writes the header with flag wx.
- loadEntriesFromFile reads 1 MiB chunks through a StringDecoder (invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD), skips malformed lines, validates the header, and appends '\n' when the last line was unterminated.
- readSessionHeader scans at most 1 MiB in 4096-byte chunks.
- Migrations: v1->v2 adds the id tree and maps firstKeptEntryIndex->firstKeptEntryId; v2->v3 renames role hookMessage->custom.

Listing.
- Concurrency limits 10 (cwd) and 64 (all); progress published every 10/100 files.
- File names sorted descending with localeCompare.
- Follows symlinked dirs but ignores links to files (#7497).

Projection (buildSessionProjection/buildSessionContext).
- The newest compaction on the branch wins; the kept range starts at firstKeptEntryId and has system messages filtered out.
- context_edit replaces an entry, or omits it when the replacement is null.
- branch_summary and custom_message become messages; labels and the session_info name are tracked.

messages.ts.
- COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX/SUFFIX and BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREFIX/SUFFIX are exact strings.
- bashExecutionToText format must match.
- convertToLlm maps custom->user, and bashExecution->user unless excludeFromContext.
- Timestamps use new Date(iso).getTime().

session-export re-parents branch entries linearly. Default output name: session-<iso with : and . replaced>.jsonl, resolved against process.cwd().

session-info-modified-timestamp calls initTheme only incidentally; drop that call in the port.

tasks.title: Settings load/merge/migrate/write with file locking; settings diagnostics; install telemetry flag
tasks.notes:
Files.
- Global: agentDir/settings.json. Project: cwd/.pi/settings.json (CONFIG_DIR_NAME).
- Settings keys are written in camelCase exactly as in the TS interface.
- Deep merge of project over global. defaultTools merges +name/-name modifiers specially.

Migrations on load:
- queueMode -> steeringMode
- websockets -> transport
- skills object -> array
- retry.maxDelayMs -> retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs
- A UTF-8 BOM is stripped (#8337).

Writes.
- Read the current file under lock, apply only the modified fields (nested-key tracking) onto the on-disk JSON, then JSON.stringify(...,null,2). This preserves unknown keys and the existing key order.
- Writes are serialized through a promise-chain write queue (flush awaits it).
- Lock: proper-lockfile lockSync(path,{realpath:false}) with 10 attempts and a 20 ms synchronous busy-wait. Share the lock helper with coding-agent-credential-stores.
- Project writes require a trusted project.
- Load/parse errors are recorded and drained (drainErrors) for diagnostics.
- The inMemory variant serializes its initial settings through the same migration.

Defaults.
- compaction: reserveTokens 16384, keepRecentTokens 20000. Per-model compaction overrides are keyed provider/modelId and validated as safe non-negative integers.
- retry: 3 attempts, base 2000 ms; provider maxRetryDelayMs defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_RETRY_DELAY_MS (60000).
- cacheWarming is global-only.
- httpIdleTimeoutMs is parsed by http-dispatcher.

Environment variables:
- VISUAL/EDITOR (fallback notepad on win32, otherwise nano)
- PI_CLEAR_ON_SHRINK
- PI_HARDWARE_CURSOR
- PI_TELEMETRY overrides enableInstallTelemetry; truthy values are 1/true/yes, case-insensitive.

The pi-tui imports are type-only (TuiMode, ScrollViewScrollbar, TerminalCapabilities, WheelScrollLines); port them as small enums.

settings-diagnostics only needs the AgentSessionRuntimeDiagnostic type. Define it in a shared types module to avoid a dependency cycle.

Test 3616 needs the DefaultResourceLoader port; 8337 also covers frontmatter BOM handling from utils.

tasks.title: auth.json AuthStorage + lock backends, config value resolution, runtime credential overlay, models-store.json, auth guidance strings
tasks.notes:
FileAuthStorageBackend.
- Creates the parent dir with mode 0700 and the file "{}" with mode 0600. The mode applies on creation only.
- Sync lock: lockSync with realpath:false, 10 attempts, 20 ms busy-wait.
- Async lock: lock({retries:0, stale:30000, onCompromised}).
  - On ELOCKED, back off min(10*2^n, 1000) * (1+random) ms, capped at the remaining time of a 30 s deadline. The sleep is abortable.
  - A compromised lock throws.
- proper-lockfile compatibility, so TS pi and the port can share ~/.pi/agent:
  - The lock is a directory `<file>.lock` created with mkdir.
  - Its mtime is refreshed every stale/2.
  - A lock is stale when its mtime is older than stale (default 10 s for the sync lock).
- Writes use JSON.stringify(data,null,2).

AuthStorage.
- A process-global read state is shared per auth path (sharedAuthFileReadState) and validated by getFileRevision = `${dev}:${ino}:${size}:${mtimeNs}:${ctimeNs}` from a bigint stat. Use MetadataExt in Rust and syscall.Stat_t in Go; Windows needs a fallback.
- Concurrent reloads are coalesced with reader counting; the reload is aborted when the reader count drops to 0.
- Without a signal, a failed read falls back to the last snapshot.
- read() resolves api_key values through resolveConfigValue(key, credential.env).
- ReadOnlyAuthStorage validates with exact messages ("Invalid auth.json: expected an object", "Invalid auth.json credential for provider \"x\"").
- InMemoryAuthStorageBackend serializes operations through a promise chain.

resolve-config-value.
- Values starting with '!' are commands. Otherwise they are templates: $NAME or ${NAME} (NAME matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), $$ -> $, $! -> !. An unterminated ${ is a literal $.
- Env lookup is `env[name] || process.env[name] || undefined`: an empty value counts as missing.
- Commands run like execSync(cmd): /bin/sh -c on Unix, 10 s timeout, stdout trimmed, stderr ignored, an empty result becomes undefined.
- On win32, run through getShellConfig (args or stdin transport) and fall back to the default shell on ENOENT.
- Results are cached per process for the cached variant.
- Error messages from resolveConfigValueOrThrow/resolveHeadersOrThrow must match exactly (tests assert them).

FileModelsStore reuses FileAuthStorageBackend on agentDir/models-store.json with the same shared read-state pattern. Reads and writes structuredClone entries.

RuntimeCredentials overlays non-persistent API keys over a CredentialStore.

auth-guidance strings join getDocsPath() with providers.md and models.md.

tasks.title: models.json schema/config, provider layer composition, remote pi.dev catalog overlay, virtual models, provider attribution headers
tasks.notes:
model-config.
- models.json is read with comments stripped (stripJsonComments) and BOM removed, then validated against the typebox schema.
- Error format: `Invalid models.json schema:\n  - <path>: <msg>\n\nFile: <path>`. The port must reproduce typebox's instance paths and messages for the tested cases.

provider-composer: getAllModels applies these layers in order:
1. Built-in provider models.
2. applyModelsJson: baseUrl and compat on all models (radius keeps its own baseUrl); custom models upserted by chat id, with defaults from findModelDefaults; defaults contextWindow 128000 and maxTokens 16384.
3. applyExtension: replace the model list, or override baseUrl only.
4. OAuth modifyModels (chat models only).
5. modelOverrides (chat models only; topmost layer).
- mergeCompat deep-merges openRouterRouting, vercelGatewayRouting, chatTemplateKwargs and chatTemplateArgs.
- All thrown error strings are asserted by model-registry tests.
- composeApiKeyAuth covers: inherited auth, configured key (env-name presence check, command values treated as configured), the default login prompt "Enter API key", headers resolved with env context, and authHeader adding `Authorization: Bearer`.
- adaptOAuth maps the legacy OAuthLoginCallbacks onto the new interaction API.
- Streaming dispatch order: extension streamSimple when model.api matches; else the base provider if it supports the api; else the global compat API registry (getApiProvider).
- Image and classifier dispatch also fall back to error results.
- configuredRequestAuthStatus sources: models_json_command, environment (with env names as the label), fallback (extension apiKey), models_json_key.

virtual-models.
- VIRTUAL_MODEL_API="pi-virtual"; the state entry customType is "pi.virtual-model-state".
- createVirtualModel maps unsupported levels to null in the thinkingLevelMap.
- withVirtualModels hides physical chat models that share an id with a virtual model; a missing provider gets a keyless provider.
- Unrouted stream error: `Virtual model p/id must be routed before streaming`.
- getBranchSelection semantics must match the tests.

remote-catalog-provider.
- Request: GET `${base}/api/models/providers/${encodeURIComponent(id)}?types=chat,image,classifier` with accept, User-Agent and if-none-match. The If-None-Match header is sent only when the stored model list is non-empty.
- 4 s per-attempt timeout via fetchWithRetry; 4 h freshness window.
- 304: only checkedAt moves. 404/501: lastModified 0, no etag. Other non-OK: persist checkedAt, then throw.
- Last-Modified is parsed like Date.parse of an RFC 1123 date; NaN becomes 0.
- The overlay applies only when lastModified > the bundled generatedAt.
- Models merge keyed by `${type}\u0000${id}`.

provider-attribution.
- openrouter: provider match or substring "openrouter.ai" in baseUrl. nvidia and cloudflare: matched by WHATWG URL hostname.
- These headers are gated by isInstallTelemetryEnabled.
- opencode session headers x-opencode-session and x-opencode-client.
- Merge order: session headers, then attribution headers, then the given sources.

Extension-provided callbacks (streamSimple, refreshModels, oauth.*, images, classifiers, route) become native trait objects.

tasks.title: ModelRuntime (pi-ai Models wrapper with auth, catalogs, virtual routing) and ModelRegistry facade; radius constants
tasks.notes:
ModelRuntime.create({credentials, modelsPath (null disables), modelsStore, allowModelNetwork}).
- Wraps pi-ai createModels with RuntimeCredentials, ModelConfig and FileModelsStore (or the in-memory store).
- Built-in providers are wrapped with withRemoteCatalog(getBuiltinModelDataGeneratedAt), except radius.
- Radius providers are created from models.json entries with oauth:"radius". The PI_RADIUS_GATEWAY override lives in radius.ts.
- Supports extension-config providers (registerProvider), native providers (registerNativeProvider) and virtual models (registerVirtualModel).
- Availability, configured and stored snapshots are guarded by sequence counters, so a stale refresh never overwrites a newer one (#7301).
- Credential operations (login/logout/modify) are serialized per provider. Raises CredentialSynchronizationError.
- PI_OFFLINE disables network refresh.
- mergeHeaders is case-insensitive, and null deletes a header.
- resolveModel routes virtual models; streamSimple on a virtual model routes with reason "direct".
- getAuth and getCompatibilityRequestConfig feed ModelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders, which maps the "authHeader requires a resolved API key" error to `No API key found for "<provider>"`.

model-registry.test.ts (2128 lines) is the main behavioural spec for models.json composition: overrides, custom models, dynamic providers, API key resolution and persistence. It covers provider-composer and model-config too.

skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/compaction-extensions.test.ts -- real Anthropic API e2e (describe.skipIf(!API_KEY))
packages/coding-agent/test/compaction-extensions-example.test.ts -- imports TS example extension examples/extensions/custom-compaction.ts; JS-extension-only
packages/coding-agent/test/trigger-compact-extension.test.ts -- imports TS example extension examples/extensions/trigger-compact.ts; JS-extension-only
tasks.notes:
Token estimation.
- estimateTokens = ceil(chars/4), where chars is the JS string .length (UTF-16 code units). Each image counts as 4800 chars. Do not use byte or char counts.
- estimateContextTokens uses the last assistant usage plus trailing estimates.
- shouldCompact: tokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens.

Cut points (findCutPoint / prepareCompaction).
- Valid cut points are user/assistant/custom message entries, never tool results.
- Split turns produce a turn-prefix summary, merged with `\n\n---\n\n**Turn Context (split turn):**\n\n`.
- Follows the recovery-omission suffix rule.
- Works with a previous compaction (iterative UPDATE prompt).

Prompts and serialization.
- File operations are tracked from read/write/edit tool calls and rendered as <read-files>/<modified-files> blocks.
- Prompt constants must be byte-identical: SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT, SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT, UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT, TURN_PREFIX_*, BRANCH_SUMMARY_*.
- serializeConversation format and truncation (UTF-16 slice) must match; nested tool call records are serialized too.

LLM call.
- completeSummarization calls completeSimple with cacheRetention "none" and sessionId ?? uuidv7(), wrapped in retryAssistantCall with the retry settings and callbacks.
- maxTokens = min(floor(0.8*reserve), model.maxTokens); the turn prefix uses 0.5; branch summaries use min(4096, ...).
- Reasoning/thinking levels are passed through (compaction-summary-reasoning test).

usage-totals: combineUsage keeps the optional cacheWrite1h/reasoning fields only when either side has them. getUsageCostBreakdown sorts by cost descending.

tasks.title: Cache warmer and cache-miss stats, nested tool calls, system prompt builder, event bus, defaults, timings, diagnostics types, experimental flag
tasks.notes:
CacheWarmer.
- Replays the last request with maxTokens 1 and maxRetries 0 before the cache TTL expires.
- delay = max(1, floor(min(0.9*ttl, ttl-10s))). TTL comes from model.promptCache[short|long]; PI_CACHE_RETENTION is read via getProviderEnvValue.
- Refresh deadline = nextWarmAt + floor((ttl-delay)/2). Age limits: 60 min while streaming, 30 min idle.
- Economics: warm if continuationProbability*missCost - warmCost >= $0.05, with continuation probability 1 while streaming and 0.15 idle.
- Anthropic budget thinking without forceAdaptiveThinking is not replayable.
- The decide hook maps to the extension cache_warming_decision event; failures fall back to pi's decision.

- _installAgentToolHooks: beforeToolCall/afterToolCall dispatch tool_call/tool_result to extensions, normalize tool-result images and record nested calls.

tasks.title: ExtensionRunner event dispatch, contexts, tool wrapper, extensions barrel
tasks.notes:
The runner owns ordered extensions, the bound runtime and contexts. Behaviors to port verbatim:

Event dispatch:
- snapshotEventHandlers copies the handler list per emit, so handlers registered during an emit do not run in that emit.
- emit(): errors are caught per handler and sent to onError listeners as {extensionPath, event, error, stack}. session_before_* stops at the first `cancel: true`.
- emitToolCall has no catch, so errors propagate to the agent loop. The first `block` short-circuits.
- emitUserBash fails closed. isUserBashEventResult requires exactly one of `operations` (with an exec fn) or `result` (output string, exitCode, cancelled, truncated, optional fullOutputPath); otherwise it throws.
- emitContext: structuredClone the messages, run the `context` handlers, then `context_with_system` with the system message restored via getCurrentSystemMessage. The leading-system-message check must use stable identity (index or id), not pointer equality.
- emitInput: chain transform results; stop on handled.
- emitBeforeAgentStart: chained systemPrompt; forceSystemPrompt; the systemPrompt getter renders via buildSystemPrompt/normalizeBuildSystemPromptOptions.
- emitMessageEnd: a replacement must keep the role.
- emitToolResult: replacing content without structuredContent deletes structuredContent.
- emitCacheWarmingDecision: the last override wins.
- emitProjectTrust: the first yes/no wins; undecided falls through.
- emitBeforeProviderRequest/Headers mutate in place.
- emitBoundary (turn_end, agent_before_settle): recreate the context after each handler; an invalid result yields empty entries.
- withUIPrompt: depth counter; ui_prompt_start/end are queued after the current task. Use a deferred task queue in Rust/Go and order them before the next await.

Registration and lookup:
- getShortcuts: RESERVED_KEYBINDINGS_FOR_EXTENSION_CONFLICTS and buildBuiltinKeybindings, keys lowercased. Diagnostics text is verbatim, e.g. "Extension shortcut '${key}' from ${path} conflicts with built-in shortcut. Skipping." Without a UI, warnings go to stderr.
- resolveRegisteredCommands: duplicates are renamed `name:N`.
- getAllRegisteredTools: first wins.

Binding and lifecycle:
- bindCore flushes queued provider and virtual-model registrations, reporting errors with event register_provider / register_virtual_model. It also installs the McpServerRegistry change listener, which emits mcp_servers_change and reportUnhandledMcpServers (event register_mcp_server).
- invalidate() marks contexts stale with the long stale message.
- createToolContext.executeTool fallback returns an isError result with the text "Nested tool calls are not available in this context" and toolCall id `${toolCallId}/0`.
- noOpUIContext defaults.

tasks.title: Agent Skills discovery/validation and prompt template loading/expansion
tasks.notes:
skills.ts:
- Name regex ^[a-z0-9-]+$, max 64 chars, no leading/trailing or double hyphens per the spec checks. Description required, max 1024.
- A SKILL.md at a directory root makes the dir a skill and stops recursion. .gitignore/.ignore/.fdignore are honored through the node-ignore matcher with path prefixing.
- Symlinked dirs and files are followed via stat. Hidden dirs and node_modules are skipped.
- Collision diagnostics keep the first loaded skill. disable-model-invocation frontmatter is respected.
- formatSkillsForPrompt XML output (escaping of & < > " ') must match byte for byte.

prompt-templates.ts:
- parseCommandArgs uses JS /\s/, i.e. Unicode whitespace including NBSP and U+FEFF, so do not use ASCII-only checks.
- substituteArgs regex /\$\{(\d+|ARGUMENTS|@):-([^}]*)\}|\$\{@:(\d+)(?::(\d+))?\}|\$(ARGUMENTS|@|\d+)/g:
  - single pass, no recursive substitution;
  - `${N:-d}` falls back when empty;
  - slice start 0 is treated as 1;
  - parseInt on huge digit strings must not panic (use saturating parse).
- Description falls back to the first non-blank body line, truncated to 60 UTF-16 code units plus "...". Rust/Go must count UTF-16 units, not bytes or chars, for parity.
- Template name is the basename minus `.md`. Directories are scanned non-recursively; broken symlinks are skipped.
- Source info: under agentDir/prompts it is user scope, under cwd/.pi/prompts project scope, otherwise local with a baseDir.
- expandPromptTemplate regex ^\/([^\s]+)(?:\s+([\s\S]*))?$ .

tasks.title: Package manager: npm/git/local sources, resource resolution, filters, install/update
tasks.notes:
A single 2760-line file. It is under the 3500-line split threshold, so it stays one unit. Natural internal seam: free functions L1-L811 (env, patterns, collectors, filters) vs the DefaultPackageManager class L812-end.

Port the command execution (runCommand, runCommandCapture, runCommandSync, spawn) behind an injectable CommandRunner trait/interface. package-manager.test.ts stubs these private methods, and the tests should assert the same argv arrays.

Resolution and precedence:
- resourcePrecedenceRank: builtin 5, package 4, project local 0 / auto 1, user local 2 / auto 3.
- resolve(): project packages first, dedupe by identity, then local entries, then auto-discovery (extensions/skills/prompts/themes plus ancestor .agents/skills up to the git root), then builtins with `-builtin:x` overrides.
- Filter patterns: plain, `!` exclude, `+` force-include, `-` force-exclude.
- matchesAnyPattern tries minimatch (default options, so dotfiles are not matched by *) against the relative path, basename and absolute posix path. For SKILL.md it also tries the parent variants.
- expandPackageGlob: fs.globSync(cwd=root), drop entries with dot segments, sort.

Sources and versions:
- parseSource: `npm:` prefix; npm spec regex ^(@?[^@]+(?:\/[^@]+)?)(?:@(.+))?$; local path detection; git URL parsing via utils/git.ts (ssh, https, shorthand).
- semver gt/maxSatisfying/rcompare/satisfies/valid/validRange use npm semantics.
- getLatestNpmVersion runs `npm view <spec> version --json`. NETWORK_TIMEOUT_MS is 10000. Update concurrency is 4.
- getPackageManagerName: detect npm, pnpm or bun from the npmCommand setting, including `--` separators and wrapper commands. Error "Ambiguous npmCommand package managers".
- Install flags:
  - npm: `--prefix <dir> --legacy-peer-deps`;
  - pnpm: config flags;
  - bun: `--cwd --omit=peer`.

On-disk layout (byte-compatible):
- Roots: agentDir/npm, agentDir/git/<host>/<path>, and tmp/extensions/<prefix>/<sha256 of `${prefix}-${suffix}${ref ? @ref : ''}`, first 8 hex chars>.
- package.json `{"name":"pi-extensions","private":true}`, pretty-printed with a 2-space indent and no trailing newline.
- .gitignore `*\n!.gitignore\n`; markPathIgnoredByCloudSync.
- Git update marker `.<name>.pi-update-incomplete`. Update sequence: fetch, reset --hard, clean -fdx, then repair missing deps.
- ls-remote runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
- resolveManagedPath refuses paths outside the root: "Refusing to use path outside package install root".
- The project scope asserts trust: "Project is not trusted; refusing to access project package storage".

Process and environment:
- spawn stdio is inherit, or [ignore, stderr, stderr] when stdout is taken over (output-guard).
- runCommandCapture error format: `${cmd} ${args} failed with code N: stderr||stdout`, or `timed out after Nms`. It resolves trimmed stdout.
- getEnv falls back to /proc/self/environ on Linux. PI_OFFLINE skips network.
- Legacy global roots: `npm root -g`, `bun pm bin -g`, `pnpm list -g --depth 0 --json`.

git-update.test.ts uses a real local git binary (no network); keep it as an integration test gated on git availability.

tasks.notes:
Lowest layer; must not import tools or extensions.

config.ts, identity:
- Reads package.json (name, version, piConfig.name/configDir) at module load. Turn these into compile-time constants generated from packages/coding-agent/package.json (Rust build.rs; Go go:embed or -ldflags -X). Still honor piConfig from PI_PACKAGE_DIR/package.json for rebranded builds.
- APP_NAME is 'pi'. APP_TITLE is 'π' unless piConfig.name is set. CONFIG_DIR_NAME is '.pi'.
- Env var names derive from APP_NAME.toUpperCase(): PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR.
- getAgentDir: the env override goes through normalizePath; otherwise join(homedir, '.pi', 'agent').
- These names must match exactly: models.json, auth.json, settings.json, themes, tools, bin, prompts, sessions, and `${APP_NAME}-debug.log`.
- getShareViewerUrl = (PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL || 'https://pi.dev/session/') + '#' + gistId. An empty env value counts as unset.

config.ts, runtime and asset detection:
- isBunBinary (import.meta.url contains $bunfs, ~BUN or %7EBUN), isBunRuntime, isBundledNode, the src-vs-dist probing in getThemesDir/getExportTemplateDir/getInteractiveAssetsDir, and getPackageDir have no meaning in a native binary.
- Embed the assets (Rust include_dir!/rust-embed; Go embed.FS) and keep PI_PACKAGE_DIR as an on-disk override.
- getReadmePath, getDocsPath, getExamplesPath and getChangelogPath are shown to the model and read with tools, so they must exist on disk. Extract them to a versioned directory or ship them next to the binary; coordinate with the system-prompt area.
- findNodePackageDir stays a pure upward fs walk: skip a dist/package.json when the parent also has one. Tested.
- getQuickJSWasmPath and setEmbeddedQuickJSWasmPath become embedded wasm bytes. resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier and getCodemodeWorkerSpecifier are removed.

config.ts, install method and self-update:
- config.test.ts fakes process.execPath and PI_PACKAGE_DIR and puts fake pnpm/yarn/bun scripts (.cmd on win32) on PATH. Port detectInstallMethod, getSelfUpdateCommand, getSelfUpdateUnavailableInstruction and getUpdateInstruction as functions that take execPath, packageDir and env.
- They shell out to `pnpm root -g`, `yarn global dir` and `bun pm bin -g`.
- The writability check uses access(W_OK): Rust rustix::fs::access, Go unix.Access.
- Display quoting wraps any arg matching /\s/ in double quotes. A renamed package gets an uninstall step joined with ' && '.
- A standalone native binary should take the 'bun-binary' branch (download instruction).

child-process.ts:
- spawnProcess and spawnProcessSync use cross-spawn on win32 only: PATHEXT lookup, and .cmd/.bat run through cmd.exe with metacharacter escaping.
- Rust: which + Command. Since 1.77 std refuses unsafe batch args, so escape explicitly or call cmd /d /s /c.
- Go: exec.LookPath plus explicit cmd /d /s /c for shims.
- waitForChildProcess (#5303):
  - Resolves on close, or after exit once both pipes reach EOF, or after a 100ms idle grace restarted on every chunk that arrives after exit.
  - Returns null for a signal exit. A spawn 'error' rejects. Streams are destroyed when it resolves.
  - Rust: pipe-reader tasks send chunk events over a channel; use select! with a resettable sleep.
  - Go: do not rely on cmd.Wait. It blocks until the pipe copiers finish when a grandchild holds the pipe. Use your own readers with time.Timer.Reset, or Cmd.WaitDelay.

paths.ts:
- normalizePath order:
  1. optional trim
  2. Unicode spaces [U+00A0, U+2000-200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000] become a space
  3. strip a leading '@'
  4. on win32, /c/x, /mnt/c/x and /cygdrive/c/x become C:\x
  5. tilde: only '~', '~/', and '~\' on win32
  6. file:// through fileURLToPath, which throws on invalid URLs. Rust url::Url::to_file_path; Go needs a hand port.
- resolvePath must match Node path.resolve: lexical . and .. handling, no trailing slash, no symlink resolution. Rust needs a hand-written lexical normalizer (std::path::absolute keeps '..'). Go filepath.Abs+Clean matches on Unix.
- getCwdRelativePath follows path.relative semantics (Rust pathdiff; Go filepath.Rel).
- getFileRevision formats dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs. It is only compared in memory (auth-storage, models-store), so any stable fingerprint works.
- markPathIgnoredByCloudSync spawns xattr (darwin) or setfattr (linux).

ansi.ts:
- The pattern comes from ansi-regex. OSC uses a lazy [\s\S]*? up to BEL, ESC-backslash or U+009C; CSI accepts ESC or U+009B. Rust regex and RE2 both support lazy quantifiers.
- Rust \d is Unicode: use [0-9].
- Keep the fast path that skips when there is no ESC or U+009B.

json.ts:
- stripJsonComments uses alternation regexes with replacement callbacks. Rust: Regex::replace_all with a closure. Go: a FindAllStringSubmatchIndex loop, because ReplaceAllStringFunc gives no access to groups.

frontmatter.ts:
- Converts CRLF and CR to LF and strips the BOM.
- The YAML is the block between a leading '---' and the first '\n---'. The body is everything 4 characters after that, then JS-trimmed. JS trim also strips U+FEFF; Rust str::trim and Go strings.TrimSpace do not, so write a JS-compatible trim.
- A null YAML document becomes {}. Parse YAML 1.2 so 'yes'/'no' stay strings.

Small helpers:
- getPiUserAgent returns `pi/${version} (${platform}; ${runtime}; ${arch})` using Node names (darwin/linux/win32, x64/arm64). Map the Rust/Go OS and arch names to these, and choose a runtime token such as rust/<ver> or go/<ver>. Check pi-user-agent.test.ts.
- sleep rejects with Error('Aborted').
- raceWithAbortSignal rejects with signal.reason or an AbortError 'The operation was aborted'. Model it with CancellationToken (Rust) or context.Context (Go) and typed errors.
- isWSL: WSL_DISTRO_NAME or WSLENV, or /proc/version matching /microsoft|wsl/i.
- fs-watch: errors must reach onError and never crash. Rust notify; Go fsnotify. FS_WATCH_RETRY_DELAY_MS is 5000.
- openBrowser never uses a shell: open, `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, or xdg-open, detached, with errors ignored.
- deprecation.ts has no importers; ask before dropping it.

tasks.title: Shell resolution, truncation, output accumulator, path utils, mutation queue, exec, output guard, ToolDefinition wrapper
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/resolve-config-value.test.ts -- belongs to the config-value/settings area (it only spies on utils/shell)
packages/coding-agent/test/rpc-prompt-response-semantics.test.ts -- belongs to the RPC area (it vi.mocks output-guard)
packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-extension.test.ts -- belongs to the MCP area. It is the only test of truncateMiddle, so add native truncateMiddle unit tests here
tasks.notes:
truncate.ts:
- Byte counts are UTF-8 (Buffer.byteLength): str.len() in Rust, len() in Go. Lines are split on '\n', and a trailing newline drops the last empty element.
- TruncationResult fields are stored in session JSONL details. Keep the camelCase names: truncated, truncatedBy ('lines', 'bytes' or null), totalLines, totalBytes, outputLines, outputBytes, lastLinePartial, firstLineExceedsLimit, maxLines, maxBytes. truncatedBy must serialize as null, not be omitted.
- truncateTail can take the end of an oversized last line, starting at a UTF-8 boundary.
- truncateLine counts UTF-16 code units (line.length, slice). Count with encode_utf16 (Rust) or the unicode/utf16 package (Go). If the cut splits a surrogate pair, JS keeps a lone surrogate that Rust/Go strings cannot hold: cut before the pair and document the divergence. The suffix is '... [truncated]'.
- truncateMiddle cuts at UTF-8 boundaries and counts removed characters in code points (Array.from). The marker is '…N chars truncated…' with U+2026.
- formatSize uses toFixed(1), which rounds exact ties up: 1280 B gives '1.3KB'. Rust {:.1} and Go strconv 'f',1 round ties to even and give '1.2KB'. Write a JS-compatible toFixed and test 1280 and 3328 bytes.

output-accumulator.ts:
- Uses a streaming TextDecoder: stateful UTF-8 that emits U+FFFD for invalid bytes and keeps split sequences across chunks. Rust: encoding_rs::Decoder or Utf8Error::error_len handling. Go: buffer bytes until utf8.FullRune.
- Keeps a rolling tail of 2x maxBytes.
- The temp file is `${prefix}-${randomBytes(8).hex}.log` in os.tmpdir(), created lazily once a limit is exceeded, with earlier chunks written first. Rust std::env::temp_dir and Go os.TempDir both honor TMPDIR.
- readFullOutput returns head and tail halves joined by '\n\n[... N bytes omitted ...]\n\n', cut at UTF-8 boundaries.
- Node write streams are async but ordered: use a buffered writer and flush it before exposing the path.

exec.ts:
- Spawns without a shell. On abort or timeout it sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5s; proc.killed only means a signal was sent.
- stdout/stderr are decoded per chunk with Buffer.toString, so multibyte characters can split. Decoding the joined buffer once is fine.
- code ?? 0: a signal-killed process reports 0 with killed=true. A spawn error resolves with code 1.
- Uses waitForChildProcess.

output-guard.ts:
- Monkey-patching process.stdout.write has no native equivalent. Add a process-wide output sink: Rust static Mutex<Box<dyn Write>>; Go a mutex-guarded io.Writer variable.
- takeOverStdout sends ordinary stdout writes to stderr. writeRawStdout keeps the real stdout for JSON/RPC protocol bytes.
- Raw writes are serialized. ENOBUFS, EAGAIN and EWOULDBLOCK retry every 10ms (Rust ErrorKind::WouldBlock; Go syscall.EAGAIN). Any other error exits with code 1.
- flushRawStdout waits for the queue to drain.
- Audit dependencies that print to stdout directly.

shell.ts:
- getShellConfig order:
  1. custom path; must exist, else 'Custom shell path not found: X'
  2. win32: %ProgramFiles% and %ProgramFiles(x86)% Git\bin\bash.exe, then `where bash.exe` (first existing line), then the multi-line 'No bash shell found' error, verbatim
  3. Unix: /bin/bash, then `which bash`, then sh
- Legacy WSL bash (C:\Windows\System32 or Sysnative\bash.exe, case-insensitive) gets args ['-s'] and stdin transport.
- getPowerShellConfig: win32 only. Prefers pwsh.exe over powershell.exe, with args -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command.
- getShellEnv prepends ~/.pi/agent/bin using whatever case the PATH key has (Windows env is case-insensitive).
- sanitizeBinaryOutput removes [\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\uFFF9-\uFFFB].
- killProcessTree on Unix: kill(-pid, SIGKILL), falling back to kill(pid). This needs the child spawned in its own group: Rust CommandExt::process_group(0); Go SysProcAttr Setpgid.
- killProcessTree on win32: spawn %SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe /F /T /PID, ignoring spawn errors (#6596; port the test with an injectable spawner).
- Tracked detached PIDs are killed on shutdown signals; the main area owns the signal handlers.

path-utils.ts:
- resolveReadPath tries, in order: the exact path; ' AM.'/' PM.' with U+202F (case-insensitive); NFD; U+2019 for straight quotes; then NFD with the curly quote. Rust: unicode-normalization. Go: x/text/unicode/norm.

file-mutation-queue.ts:
- Keyed by realpath. Falls back to path.resolve on ENOENT or ENOTDIR and rethrows other errors. Symlink aliases share one queue.
- Registration is itself serialized, which keeps the order FIFO.
- Rust: a global map of Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>> (FIFO-fair), removing the entry after the last release. Go: a per-key FIFO built from chained channels, because sync.Mutex is not FIFO.
- The lock stays held until fn settles.

tool-definition-wrapper.ts:
- Provides wrapToolDefinition(s) and createToolDefinitionFromAgentTool, with lazy ctxFactory.
- Define the ToolDefinition trait/interface in a leaf module that does not import extensions. Go forbids the extensions/types.ts <-> tools import cycle.

tasks.title: Image sniffing, EXIF, resize/convert pipeline and clipboard backends
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard-image-native-errors.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive-mode area (drives InteractiveMode)
packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard-paste-file-paths.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive-mode area (drives InteractiveMode)
tasks.notes:
mime.ts:
- Sniffs magic bytes from the start of the buffer or file: JPEG FF D8 FF, the PNG signature, GIF87a/89a, RIFF....WEBP, and BMP 'BM'.
- APNG (an acTL chunk) is not a supported PNG. Keep the rules exact.

photon.ts:
- Lazily loads photon-node WASM and patches fs.readFileSync for Bun binaries. Drop it entirely and use native codecs.
- Rust: the image crate with png, jpeg, gif, webp and bmp, and imageops Lanczos3 or fast_image_resize. photon-rs gives identical algorithms.
- Go: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, x/image/webp, x/image/bmp, plus disintegration/imaging Lanczos.

exif-orientation.ts:
- Hand-parses JPEG APP1 Exif and WebP EXIF chunks: TIFF byte order, IFD0 tag 0x0112. Orientations 2-8 map to flips and rotations.
- Port the byte parser directly and keep the silent fallback on malformed data.

image-resize-core.ts:
- Defaults: maxWidth and maxHeight 2000, maxBytes 4.5MB measured as base64 length (4*ceil(n/3)), jpegQuality 80.
- Tries the original first. Then, at each size, tries PNG and JPEG with deduplicated quality steps [q, 85, 70, 55, 40], then scales by 0.75 and repeats. Returns a failure when nothing fits.
- Encoded bytes will differ from photon. Tests should assert dimensions, MIME type and limits, not bytes.

image-resize.ts and image-resize-worker.ts:
- Resizing runs in a worker_threads Worker with an in-process fallback. Replace both with spawn_blocking (Rust) or a goroutine (Go).
- formatDimensionNote produces '[Image: original WxH, displayed at wxh. Multiply coordinates by S to map to original image.]'. S uses toFixed(2), with the same tie-rounding hazard as formatSize.

image-process.ts and tool-result-images.ts:
- image-process converts GIF, WebP and BMP to PNG (image-convert), then resizes with the model's ModelImageResizeOptions.
- tool-result-images rewrites ImageContent blocks and appends a text block of hints joined with '\n'.

clipboard-command.ts:
- An async spawn with a timeout and buffered stdout. Rust: tokio::process with timeout. Go: exec.CommandContext.

clipboard.ts:
- copyToClipboard writes directly first (the native addon, then platform commands), then OSC 52.
- Platform commands, kept in source order: pbcopy (darwin); Windows clipboard through PowerShell reading a temp file, with wslpath -w under WSL; termux-clipboard-set when TERMUX_VERSION is set; wl-copy when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set; xclip -selection clipboard; xsel --clipboard --input.
- OSC 52 is ESC]52;c;<base64>BEL, skipped when the encoded text exceeds 100000 characters. It is preferred under WT_SESSION and emitted for remote or headless sessions.
- The error messages ('Clipboard unavailable: ...') are verbatim.
- The OSC 52 write goes to process.stdout and must go through the output-guard sink.
- readClipboardText uses termux-clipboard-get, `wl-paste --no-newline --type text`, xclip -out or xsel --output. readClipboardFilePaths reads file paths from the clipboard.

clipboard-image.ts:
- Tries the native addon first.
- Wayland: `wl-paste --list-types`, pick a supported image type, then `wl-paste --type T --no-newline`.
- X11: `xclip -selection clipboard -t TARGETS -o`, then the preferred type.
- WSL: a powershell.exe script saves the image to a temp PNG, located through wslpath.
- BMP is converted to PNG.
- isWaylandSession checks env. extensionForImageMimeType maps MIME types to file extensions.

Testing and native clipboard:
- The tests vi.mock child_process, the pi-tui native clipboard, process.platform and env. Define a ClipboardBackend trait/interface (command runner, native clipboard, platform, env, temp fs) and inject it.
- Native clipboard: Rust arboard (with wayland-data-control). Go golang.design/x/clipboard (cgo); without it, use the command fallbacks only.

tasks.title: fetchWithRetry, fd/rg tools-manager, version check, git URL parsing, changelog, zip writer, Windows self-update
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/bug-report.test.ts -- belongs to the bug-report area, which uses zip.ts indirectly
tasks.notes:
management-http.ts, fetchWithRetry:
- maxRetries defaults to 2 (non-finite also means 2).
- Retries on status 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 (unless retryOnStatus=false), cancelling the discarded body. Also retries transport errors.
- Caller abort and the overall timeoutMs are terminal. attemptTimeoutMs aborts only the current attempt.
- An AbortError is not retried unless an attempt timeout caused it.
- Rust: reqwest with a per-request timeout plus a tokio::time::timeout for the overall budget, and a CancellationToken.
- Go: net/http with nested context.WithTimeout.
- Inject an HTTP client trait/interface; the tests stub the global fetch. Should honor the same proxy env as the http-dispatcher area.

tools-manager.ts:
- TOOLS_DIR = getBinDir() is evaluated at module load. Compute it lazily but read the env the same way.
- getToolPath checks ~/.pi/agent/bin/<bin>(.exe) first. Otherwise it probes `<name> --version` on PATH (fd also tries fdfind) and returns the bare command name.
- getLatestVersion requests https://github.com/<repo>/releases/latest with redirect 'manual' and parses the tag from Location: resolve relative Locations, discard the body, and keep the error messages verbatim. Rust: reqwest redirect::Policy::none(). Go: CheckRedirect returning http.ErrUseLastResponse.
- Asset names use darwin/linux/win32 and x86_64/aarch64 (musl on Linux, msvc zip on Windows). fd is pinned to 10.3.0 on darwin x64. Timeouts: 10s network, 120s download.
- Extraction uses tar or unzip, and on Windows System32 tar.exe then PowerShell Expand-Archive. Native extraction is equivalent and removes the external tools: Rust flate2+tar / zip; Go archive/tar, compress/gzip, archive/zip. Then chmod 755 and rename into the bin dir.
- PI_OFFLINE ('1', 'true' or 'yes', case-insensitive) disables downloads. Android prints a Termux `pkg install` hint. Status goes through a callback, never the console. The error cause chain is surfaced (tested).

version-check.ts:
- Fetches https://pi.dev/api/latest-version with the pi user agent.
- PI_OFFLINE and PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK short-circuit.
- Uses semver valid() and compare(). If either version is invalid, any trimmed difference counts as newer.
- formatVersionCheckError appends error codes collected from error.cause and AggregateError, or the cause message. Native errors need an equivalent cause chain; adapt test expectations to native error codes.

git.ts, parseGitUrl:
- Built on hosted-git-info.fromUrl plus custom handling: git+ssh://, scp-like git@host:path, https URLs, an optional #ref or @ref, and github: shortcuts.
- The GitSource objects are persisted in settings.json package sources, so their shape must be identical. Hand-port the needed hosted-git-info patterns; git-ssh-url.test.ts is the spec.

changelog.ts:
- Parses '## [x.y.z]' sections. compareVersions is numeric. getNewEntries filters by lastVersion. getChangelogPath is re-exported from config.
- normalizeChangelogLinks rewrites inline markdown links:
  - LEGACY_REPO_RE has a lookahead (?=\/|$), which Rust regex and Go RE2 lack. Capture the boundary group and re-emit it, or check it by hand.
  - It also uses path.posix.normalize and encodeURI (no stdlib equivalent; hand-port the JS reserved set).
  - Links are rewritten to blob/tree at tag v<version>.

zip.ts:
- A minimal ZIP writer: local headers, central directory and EOCD, with deflateRawSync and crc32.
- DOS date and time come from local time. Rust: flate2 DeflateEncoder, crc32fast, and chrono::Local (the time crate's local offset is unreliable on multithreaded Unix). Go: compress/flate, hash/crc32, time.Local.
- Compressed bytes may differ.

windows-self-update.ts:
- Before an npm self-update on win32, renames loaded .node addons (from process.report.getReport().sharedObjects under the install dir) aside so npm can replace locked files.
- A native binary loads no .node addons. Replace this with renaming the running .exe for standalone self-update, or make it a no-op.

tasks.title: edit-diff engine and the edit, write, read, ls tools
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/image-resize-callers.test.ts#L46-55 -- covers processFileArguments in the CLI file-processor area
packages/coding-agent/test/image-resize-callers.test.ts#L86-95 -- covers deferred attachment resizing in the CLI/agent-session area
tasks.notes:
edit-diff.ts, text handling:
- Detects CRLF vs LF from the first line ending, normalizes to LF, and restores the original endings afterward. The BOM is split with splitBom and put back.
- normalizeForFuzzyMatch applies NFKC, strips trailing whitespace per line, and folds smart single/double quotes, Unicode dashes and Unicode spaces to ASCII.
- JS uses UTF-16 indices. Use byte offsets on the normalized string consistently. NFKC changes lengths, which is why applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines maps by line: only lines touched by a replacement take normalized text; all other lines keep their original bytes.
- Validation errors (empty oldText, not found, multiple occurrences, overlap, no change) are seen by the model and asserted in tests: copy them verbatim.

edit-diff.ts, diff and patch:
- generateDiffString runs jsdiff diffLines. Lines are prefixed '+', '-' or ' ' with padded line numbers. Context is 4 lines, with '...' marking gaps. It also returns firstChangedLine.
- The patch is createTwoFilesPatch(path, path, old, new, ..., {context: 4}) with the Index/=== header removed.
- Both strings are stored in EditToolDetails (session JSONL) and tests apply the patch with applyPatch.
- Hand-port jsdiff 8.0.4: the base Myers diff with the line tokenizer, which keeps newlines in tokens; structuredPatch hunk assembly; formatPatch including '\ No newline at end of file'; and applyPatch.
- Rust similar and Go difflib choose different hunks on ambiguous diffs.
- computeEditsDiff is also called by renderers/edit.ts for previews.

edit.ts:
- Schema {path, edits: [{oldText, newText}]}, constrainedSampling strict 'prefer', renderShell 'self'.
- prepareArguments accepts edits as a JSON string, as a single object, or as legacy top-level oldText/newText. Keep the precedence.
- Errors: 'Edit tool input is invalid. edits must contain at least one replacement.' and `Could not edit file: ${path}. ${msg}.`. Success text: `Successfully replaced ${n} block(s) in ${path}.`.
- Reads decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement (Rust from_utf8_lossy; Go strings.ToValidUTF8).
- After each await, check abort and throw 'Operation aborted', but keep the queue lock until the in-flight I/O settles. The deferred-promise tests rely on this.

write.ts:
- mkdir -p, then write UTF-8. Success text is `Successfully wrote to ${path}` using the user-supplied path.

read.ts:
- Resolves with resolveReadPathAsync. Images are detected by magic bytes and run through processImage with the model's resize options; when resizing is unsafe the result is text-only.
- Text is split on '\n'. offset is 1-based. Then truncateHead.
- Notices are verbatim: '[Showing lines a-b of N. Use offset=M to continue.]', the '(50.0KB limit)' variant, '[K more lines in file. Use offset=M to continue.]', and '[Line N is X, exceeds 50.0KB limit. Use bash: sed -n 'Np' path | head -c 51200]'.
- Offset errors are verbatim: `Offset ${offset} is beyond end of file (${n} lines total)`.

ls.ts:
- Sorts with a.toLowerCase().localeCompare(b.toLowerCase()), which is ICU root collation: Rust feruca or icu_collator; Go golang.org/x/text/collate (language.Und). A plain codepoint sort differs for accented names and punctuation.
- Directories get a '/' suffix via stat, which follows symlinks; stat failures skip the entry. Dotfiles are included.
- Default limit 500. Notices: `${limit} entries limit reached. Use limit=${2*limit} for more` and '50.0KB limit reached'. An empty directory gives '(empty directory)'.
- Errors: `Path not found`, `Not a directory`, and `Cannot read directory: ${e.message}`. The last embeds Node's errno text, which native code cannot reproduce; map errno to Node-style messages or relax the tests.

Operations interfaces:
- ReadOperations, EditOperations, WriteOperations and LsOperations become async traits/interfaces for remote backends.
- Details structs (EditToolDetails, ReadToolDetails, LsToolDetails) go in the leaf tool-types module, so renderers and extensions can import them without cycles.

tasks.title: bash and powershell tools, bash-executor, find and grep tools, tools index
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-bash-persistence.test.ts -- belongs to the agent-session area (exercises bash-executor through AgentSession)
packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/9068-user-bash-fail-closed.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive/RPC area
packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/8611-thinking-toggle-pending-bash-output.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive components area
tasks.notes:
bash.ts, schema and timeouts:
- Schema {command, timeout?: number in seconds}.
- The description embeds DEFAULT_MAX_LINES and '50KB'.
- outputSchema {output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds} uses snake_case and is consumed by codemode. Serialize wall_time_seconds exactly as JS would: serde_json prints 2.0 where JS prints 2.
- A non-finite or non-positive timeout fails with 'Invalid timeout: must be a finite number of seconds'. Above 2147483647 ms it fails with 'Invalid timeout: maximum is 2147483.647 seconds'.
- The JS Number-to-string formatting of the seconds also appears in 'Command timed out after N seconds'.

bash.ts, local operations:
- Checks the cwd first: `Working directory does not exist: ${cwd}\nCannot execute ${shellName} commands.`.
- Spawns shell, args and command; legacy WSL bash gets the command on stdin and ignores stdin errors.
- Non-win32 children are detached into their own process group, and the PID is tracked for shutdown.
- stdout and stderr are delivered in arrival order through one onData.
- Abort or timeout kills the process tree and rejects with 'aborted' or `timeout:${secs}`.
- Exit code = code ?? (signal ? 128 + signo : 1). Rust ExitStatusExt::signal; Go WaitStatus.Signal(). Use the libc signal numbers, which match Node's os.constants.signals.

bash.ts, environment:
- Removes PI_SESSION_ID, PI_SESSION_FILE, PI_PROVIDER, PI_MODEL and PI_REASONING_LEVEL from the env, then sets them from ctx when exposeSessionEnvironment is true (the default). promptGuidelines are only included when it is on.
- spawnHook may rewrite {command, cwd, env}. commandPrefix is prepended with '\n'.

bash.ts, execute:
- Output goes into an OutputAccumulator. onUpdate is called once with empty content, then throttled to BASH_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS (100, from renderers/bash.ts): leading edge plus a trailing timer.
- Output arriving after completion is dropped (#5208).
- Errors are thrown as appendStatus(output, 'Command aborted' / 'Command timed out after N seconds' / 'Command exited with code N' / 'Command terminated without an exit code'), so the model sees the output.
- structuredContent.output is capped at 1 MiB with truncateMiddle.
- Windows: there are no process groups, so use taskkill /T. bash-close-hang-windows covers daemonized descendants (cfg(windows) only).

powershell.ts:
- Reuses createShellToolDefinition with getPowerShellConfig, which only exists on win32.

find.ts:
- Default limit 1000. A custom FindOperations.glob path gets ignore ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**'].
- Otherwise it calls ensureTool('fd'). Failure: 'fd is not available and could not be downloaded'.
- fd args: --glob --color=never --hidden.
- Adds --no-require-git unless a .git exists in any ancestor (#5960), then --max-results.
- A pattern containing '/' adds --full-path and gets a '**/' prefix unless it starts with '/' or '**/' or is '**'. On win32, '/' becomes [/\\].
- The command ends with '--', pattern, searchPath. fd's exact glob and .gitignore semantics are what you want (#3302, #3303), so always spawn fd; do not reimplement globbing.
- relativizeFindResultPath handles root and drive-root search paths (#6104).
- Messages: 'No files found matching pattern'; `${limit} results limit reached. Use limit=${2*limit} for more, or refine pattern`; `Failed to run fd: ${err.message}`.

grep.ts:
- Default limit 100 (minimum 1). Calls ensureTool('rg').
- Runs `rg --json --line-number --color=never --hidden` with optional --ignore-case, --fixed-strings and --glob.
- Parses JSON-lines 'match' events. path.text can instead be base64 path.bytes for non-UTF-8 names.
- Kills rg once the limit is reached (matchLimitReached).
- Context lines are read from the file itself.
- Output lines are 'path:N: text' for matches and 'path-N- text' for context. truncateLine applies at 500 UTF-16 units (linesTruncated), then truncateHead.
- rg exit 1 means 'No matches found'.
- Messages: `${limit} matches limit reached. Use limit=${2*limit} for more, or refine pattern`; 'ripgrep (rg) is not available and could not be downloaded'.

bash-executor.ts (user '!' commands):
- Streaming decode, then stripAnsi, sanitizeBinaryOutput, and removal of '\r'.
- The rolling buffer is measured in UTF-16 text.length (2x50KB), while totalBytes counts raw bytes. The temp file pi-bash-<hex>.log opens once raw bytes exceed 50KB or the final output is truncated.
- cancelled means exitCode is undefined.
- BashResult {output, exitCode, cancelled, truncated, fullOutputPath} is persisted in bashExecution session entries. Keep the field names and omit undefined fields; Go omitempty would also drop exitCode 0, so use pointers.

syntax-highlight.ts:
- highlight.js 10.7.3 core with 21 eager languages: bash, c, cpp, csharp, dart, go, groovy, java, javascript, json, kotlin, lua, nix, perl, php, python, ruby, rust, scala, swift, typescript. loadAllHighlightLanguages dynamically imports the rest.
- highlight(code, {language, theme}) passes hljs HTML through renderHighlightedHtml, which walks nested <span class='hljs-X'>.

  - Entities are decoded by html.ts.

Map their scopes or token types to hljs scope names (keyword, built_in, type, literal, number, string, comment, title, title.class, title.function, params, attr, meta, variable, ...) so the theme.ts mappings and the cli-highlight default-scope test keep working.

tasks.notes:
Rust: modes::interactive::theme::{theme, theme_json, system_theme, theme_controller}. Go: package interactive/theme. Build this unit first; most of the coding-agent crate depends on it.

Global state:
- The TS `theme` export is a Proxy over globalThis[Symbol.for('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent:theme')]; the legacy @mariozechner key exists only for duplicate JS module copies. Natively use one global: Rust ArcSwap<Theme> or RwLock<Arc<Theme>> behind fn theme() -> Arc<Theme>; Go atomic.Pointer[Theme].
- onThemeChange listeners are a Vec of boxed callbacks. Registered themes come from extensions or the resource loader.
- Terminal colors and color scheme are separate globals. setTerminalColors uses identity checks to invalidate the lazy color cache.

Byte parity:
- fg/bg use precomputed ANSI per mode (truecolor/256 via getTerminalColorMode).
- Token "" emits \x1b[39m / \x1b[49m.
- Dim fg: `${ansi}\x1b[2m${text}\x1b[22;39m`. Dim bg: `${ansi}${text}\x1b[49m`.
- bold/italic/underline/inverse/strikethrough go through chalk 6. Hand-port chalk's applyStyle: replace inner close codes with the open code and wrap \n / \r\n with close+open. Port its supports-color level detection (FORCE_COLOR, NO_COLOR, TTY, TERM=dumb, CI); level 0 returns plain text.
- Appearance detection uses average OKLab L of concrete colors, excluding palette indices 0-15.

Theme JSON:
- Fields: name (may not contain '/'), $schema, vars, colors (camelCase tokens), optional export {pageBg, cardBg, infoBg}.
- Literals: number 0-255, "", #hex, and /^ok(lch|hsl)\(/i strings. Var refs resolve recursively, with an exact error message for circular refs.
- Fallbacks: scrollbarTrack->muted, scrollbarThumb->text, thinkingMax->thinkingXhigh, searchMatchBg->selectedBg, searchMatchText->text.
- BACKGROUND_TOKENS: selectedBg, searchMatchBg, userMessageBg, customMessageBg, toolPendingBg, toolSuccessBg, toolErrorBg.
- Validation error text must match exactly: 'Missing required color tokens:' (sorted), then 'Other errors:' with lines `  - ${instancePath||'/'}: ${message}`, using typebox's message wording.
- TS validation is opt-in via setThemeJsonValidator to save ~17MB of imports. Natively, always validate; keep the setter as a no-op or remove it.

Loading:
- Built-ins are read from getThemesDir(). Embed dark/light with include_str!/go:embed, but getAvailableThemesWithPaths still reports a path (config.ts layout); decide on a virtual path.
- Ordering: 'system' first, then localeCompare; use ICU-like collation, not byte order.
- theme-schema.json is not loaded at runtime; ship it as a copied asset.

Watcher:
- fs.watch on the custom themes dir with a 100ms debounce and stale-timer guard. Reload the active custom theme; fall back to dark on deletion.
- On error, close the watcher (#2791). Use notify / fsnotify.

Terminal detection:
- parseAutoThemeSetting('light/dark') and resolveThemeSetting.
- detectColorFgBgTheme takes the last COLORFGBG field; 0-6 and 8 are dark.
- Priority: reported background, then scheme, then COLORFGBG, then dark.
- markTerminalColorsPending makes the system theme grayscale (saturation 0).

system-theme.ts:
- Float math must match JS: Math.round is half-up toward +inf, unlike Rust f64::round and Go math.Round (away from zero); use floor(x+0.5).
- Port the degree-5 polynomial coefficients, 20-iteration bisection, WCAG luminance and hex formatting (toString(16).padStart(2,'0')) verbatim.

theme-controller.ts:
- TERMINAL_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS=100. Late replies are applied through onLateReply. Merge with previous colors and skip the re-render when equal.
- Mode 2031 scheme notifications are enabled only for auto pairs or the system theme. The '<in-memory>' theme name is used for preview. rebindTui is called after a renderer swap.

Other:
- highlightCode/getMarkdownTheme map highlight.js scope classes to theme tokens (cli-highlight style); this depends on the utils/syntax-highlight port producing the same token classes.
- getLanguageFromPath extension map: port verbatim.
- getThemeExportColors converts okhsl to hex for CSS and numbers to hex via indexedColor (#5596).
- Test sharing: max-thinking.test.ts is shared with cli/args; syntax-highlight.test.ts only for its 'theme syntax highlighting' describe (rest belongs to utils).

Struct design:
- All six interactive-mode units are impl blocks / methods on ONE struct. Group fields into sub-structs (ui handle, containers, editor state, queues, extension-UI state, selector state, lifecycle flags) to limit borrow conflicts.
- Prefer single-threaded UI ownership: Rust Rc<RefCell<..>> on a LocalSet, or an mpsc command loop; Go confines all UI mutation to one goroutine and sends events over channels.
- Expose narrow traits/interfaces (SessionPort, RuntimeHost, UiPort, SettingsPort, ProcessControl, CommandRunner, Clipboard, Clock). Tests then build a real InteractiveMode with fakes instead of TS prototype.call(fakeThis).

Constructor:
- setCapabilityOverrides from settings; runtimeHost hooks (rebind and render callbacks).

2. Changelog and scope line.

5. ui.start.

- rebuildChatFromMessages; renderProjectTrustWarningIfNeeded; getUserInput resolves a pending promise (oneshot channel).

Shutdown:
- Signal path (SIGTERM, plus SIGHUP on non-win32; listeners prepended): dispose extensions (session_shutdown), disable auto-sync, drainInput(1000ms), ui.stop, exit 0. Handlers stay registered until cleanup finishes (#5724). No resume hint.
- Interactive path: disable auto-sync, drain, stop, dispose, print the resume hint (formatResumeCommand) for persisted sessions, exit 0.
- Re-entrant shutdown is a no-op (#5080).
- emergencyTerminalExit uses code 129 on EIO/EPIPE/ENOTCONN from stdout/stderr.
- The uncaughtException handler records a crash. Natively use a panic hook plus explicit error paths.

Ctrl+Z (non-win32):
- Ignore SIGINT; register a one-shot SIGCONT handler that restores (ui.start, requestRender(true)); ui.stop; kill(0, SIGTSTP); clean up if it throws.
- The setInterval(2**30) keepalive exists only to keep the JS event loop alive; it is not needed natively.
- win32 shows a status message instead.
- Use signal-hook/nix (Rust) or os/signal + syscall.Kill(0, SIGTSTP) (Go) behind a ProcessControl seam so tests can assert calls.

Queues and expansion:
- Steering and follow-up queues; dequeue restores to the editor; compaction queue flush; pending bash components flush after streaming.
- handleOpenExternalEditor: $VISUAL then $EDITOR; ui.stop before, ui.start + requestRender(true) after.
- Thinking/model cycling, tool output expansion and thinking block visibility rebuild the chat.

tasks.title: Interactive components foundation: borders, key hints, status indicators, custom editor, diff, mermaid
tasks.notes:
This unit must stay free of dependencies on other component units and on core/tools renderers. Core tool renderers, the codemode/llama/mcp extension UIs and the experimental TUIs import dynamic-border, keybinding-hints, visual-truncate and diff.

**keybinding-hints**
- On process.platform darwin, 'alt' is shown as 'option' (capitalized form 'Option').
- Bindings joined with '/'.
- keyHint = dim key + muted description.

**countdown-timer**
- remaining = ceil(ms/1000).
- onTick fires immediately, then every 1000ms with requestRender.
- onExpire fires at 0.
- dispose clears the interval.

**visual-truncate**
- Renders through a temporary pi-tui Text and keeps the last N visual lines.
- VisualLinePreview caches per width.

**markdown-transform**
- Chains transformers in order, swallows exceptions and ignores non-string returns.
- Native transformer signature: Result<String> or (string, error).

**status-indicator**
- Subclasses of Loader carrying a kind.
- Retry wraps CountdownTimer.
- Compaction labels differ for manual / threshold / overflow.
- renderInBorder / renderSpinnerInBorder are consumed by CustomEditor.
- IdleStatus renders 2 blank lines to keep the vertical layout stable.

**custom-editor**
Extends pi-tui Editor, so the native Editor needs overridable hooks (a handler trait or composition). Key dispatch order is exact and tested:
1. onExtensionShortcut
2. pasteImage
3. interrupt (skipped while autocomplete is showing)
4. exit (only when the text is empty)
5. history bindings (take precedence)
6. actionHandlers map

The top border embeds the status with ' ↑ N more ' overflow math.

**diff.ts**
- Line regex /^([+-\s])(\s*\d*)\s(.*)$/.
- Tabs become 3 spaces.
- Intra-line word diff (jsdiff diffWords, highlighted with theme.inverse) applies only when exactly one removed line pairs with one added line.
- Leading whitespace is stripped from the first change.

**mermaid.ts**
Flow:
- Marked().lexer finds top-level code tokens with lang mermaid.
- Each token.raw is replaced by grok-mermaid render() rows. Each row becomes an inline code span whose backtick fence is longer than the longest backtick run in the row; empty rows use nbsp; rows are joined with two spaces + newline.
- Warnings render only when not streaming.
- Span classes (border/text/edge/edgeLabel/title) map to theme colors.

The transformer is skipped when:
- mode is off;
- messageType is thinking;
- the message is streaming and mode != 'streaming'.

**pi-logo**
- Exact RGB constants: CORAL 228,138,122; BLUE 79,142,179; YELLOW 234,182,93.
- Half-block glyphs.
- supportsPiLogo = !isAppleTerminalSession().

tasks.title: Print/JSON event mode, RPC JSONL mode, RPC types and RpcClient
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/rpc.test.ts -- e2e: requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and spawns built dist/cli.js against a real provider
packages/coding-agent/test/rpc-example.ts -- manual interactive script driving a real provider, not a test
tasks.notes:
jsonl.ts:
- Split on LF only, using a streaming UTF-8 decoder so multi-byte characters survive chunk boundaries. Strip one trailing \r. Never split on U+2028/2029.
- serializeJsonLine = JSON.stringify(value) + "\n".
- Natively, use BufRead::read_until(b'\n') / bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n'), with the final unterminated line flushed on EOF.

JSON output must match JSON.stringify:
- Key insertion order: use structs, or serde_json with preserve_order.
- No escaping of U+2028/2029, '<', '>' or '&'. Go's encoding/json always escapes U+2028/2029, so use a custom encoder or encoding/json/v2 with HTML escaping off.
- JS number formatting: integers without .0, shortest round-trip floats. In Rust use ryu-js.
- Omit undefined fields instead of writing null.

json-event.toJsonEvent:
- message_update becomes {type, usage, assistantMessageEvent} with `partial` removed.
- toolcall_start gains id and toolName (#7925).
- Usage stays on message_update (#7911). Output stays linear, never buffered out of order (#7290).

print-mode:
- JSON mode writes the session header line first.
- Text mode prints the last assistant text. On stopReason error/aborted, print the message to stderr and exit 1.
- SIGTERM exits 143; SIGHUP exits 129 (non-Windows).
- runtimeHost.dispose emits session_shutdown exactly once.
- Respect stdout backpressure (writeRawStdout / waitForRawStdoutBackpressure).

rpc-mode:
- Calls takeOverStdout.
- Must handle input lines concurrently: spawn a task or goroutine per line. Reason: extension_ui_response must resolve pending dialogs while a prompt preflight is still awaiting them.
- Response shapes:
  - success: {id?, type:"response", command, success:true, data?}
  - failure: {id?, type:"response", command, success:false, error}
  - parse failures: command "parse" with text "Failed to parse command: <msg>". The <msg> suffix is V8-specific and cannot match natively; document it.
- An unknown command echoes its id (#5868).
- The prompt response is sent only after preflight, with a disposition.
- Extension UI requests use UUIDv4 ids.
- user_bash hooks fail closed (#9068). That test also has an interactive part owned by interactive-mode.
- Shutdown on stdin end, signal (143/129), or extension shutdown request. Skip the stdout flush on SIGTERM.

rpc-client:
- Spawns the native pi binary (not node).
- Ids are req_N; default timeout 30 s.
- Pending requests are rejected with `Agent process exited (code=43 signal=null)`. Go and Rust have to synthesize the `null` text.
- stop() sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 1 s.
- waitForIdle and promptAndWait resolve on agent_settled.
- Tests that use node child scripts should use `sh -c 'exit 43'` or a tiny test helper binary.

rpc-prompt-response-semantics.test mocks output-guard/jsonl/theme. Natively, inject the writer through a trait or interface.

tasks.title: Experimental internal process spawning, coordinator socket router, Session catalog
tasks.notes:
process.ts: INTERNAL_PROCESS_ENV="__PI_INTERNAL_SPAWN" with roles coordinator|server|session-worker. consumeInternalProcessRole deletes the env var at startup so grandchildren do not inherit it.
- spawnInternalProcess spawns process.execPath [--import source-resolver.ts when running from .ts] entryUrl args, with detached:true, stdio ignore, windowsHide, cwd=process.cwd(), then unref().
- Native: re-exec std::env::current_exe() / os.Executable() with the role env.
  - Rust: Command::new(exe).env(..).stdin/stdout/stderr(Stdio::null()) plus CommandExt::process_group(0) (or setsid in pre_exec). Do not block on the child; reap it in a detached thread so no zombie remains while the parent lives.
  - Go: exec.Command with SysProcAttr{Setsid:true}, Start, then go cmd.Wait().
- terminateInternalProcess sends SIGKILL and awaits exit.
- defaultEntryUrl (dist/bundle/coordinator.js or cli.js) and source-resolver.ts (Node module.registerHooks tsconfig-path loader) have no native equivalent. Do not port source-resolver; coordinator-entry.ts becomes a role branch in main().

coordinator.ts, wire format:
- JSON lines, encodeControlLine = JSON.stringify(msg)+"\n", max line 128 MiB (MAX_CONTROL_LINE_BYTES). Reject or close on overflow.
- Messages are typebox Type.Object (extra properties allowed, unlike the worker protocol's StrictObject). Use serde internally tagged enums, #[serde(tag="type")], with camelCase fields (serverConnectionId, peerId, endpoint, protocol, peers, from, to, payload). payload is arbitrary JSON: serde_json::Value / json.RawMessage.
- COORDINATOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION=3. The peerId "server" is reserved. Only the server may broadcast.

coordinator.ts, coordinator process:
- The coordinator's module-global state should become a struct.
- Sockets: public `<dir>/<serverId>.sock`, control `<dir>/control-<serverId>.sock`, both chmod 0600 except on win32. Server endpoints are `server-<serverId>-<12 hex>.sock`.
- Public connections are piped bidirectionally to the current server endpoint (tokio::io::copy_bidirectional / two io.Copy goroutines). They are all closed when the server is replaced.
- Stale socket removal: lstat isSocket plus a connect probe. ECONNREFUSED or ENOENT means stale, so unlink.
- Empty shutdown: 30s after startup, otherwise 250ms. cleanupSocket is skipped on win32.
- ensureCoordinator spawns and retries connect every 10ms for up to 10s.
- macOS sun_path is limited to 104 bytes; long PI_SERVER_DIR paths fail the same way TS does.

session-catalog.ts:
- meta.json is exactly JSON.stringify({createdAt:<ms number>, cwd}, null, "\t")+"\n". Use serde_json PrettyFormatter::with_indent(b"\t"); in Go use json.Encoder with SetIndent("","\t") and SetEscapeHTML(false), and note that Go escapes U+2028/U+2029.
- Session id regex ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$. The default id is lowercase randomUUID (uuid v4).
- createSession maps an EEXIST mkdir to "Session <id> already exists". readSession tolerates missing or invalid metadata (it returns undefined).

tasks.title: Experimental chord service contracts and providers (agent controller, models, slash commands, transcript, sessions, plugins, connection sources)
tasks.notes:
Service contracts (defineService) become Rust traits / Go interfaces from the native chord port. Service ids must stay byte-identical because they travel on the CBOR protocol: pi.agent-controller, pi.models, pi.presentation-plugins, pi.session-plugins, pi.session-directory, pi.session-management, pi.transcript, plus local-only pi.local.presentation-ui and pi.local.slash-commands. Keep member names and argument/result JSON shapes exactly.

AgentController results:
- {accepted:boolean, operationId|entryId, error:{code:"busy"|"operation_failed", message}|null}. The busy path comes from durable ConversationBusy.
- waitForPrompt returns {status:"done",text,reason:null} | {status:"unanswered",text:null,reason}.
- cancelQueued outcomes: cancelled / already_consumed / not_found.
- parseSubmissionId uses regex ^[1-9][0-9]*$. Submission ids are positive JS safe integers: use u64 with a check of <= 2^53-1.

Models state:
- {catalog:{revision, availableModels:[{provider, modelId, name, reasoning}]}, configuration:{model|null, thinkingLevel}}, plus refresh.
- select persists the default model through SettingsManager (settings.json byte compatibility is owned by the settings area).

Slash commands:
- Name regex ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:-]*$ (u flag; ASCII only, so no unicode issue).
- Registry replace is staged.
- Builtins: /model, /thinking (THINKING_DESCRIPTIONS text), /compact, /reload.

services/server.ts:
- The replicated SessionDirectory {revision, sessions} uses serialized mutations, via a promise tail: use a tokio Mutex or a Go channel worker to keep FIFO order.
- Each client gets a RemoteServiceProvider.

services/connection.ts:
- ServerServiceSourceImpl states: connecting/connected/disconnected. SessionServiceSourceImpl states: detached/attaching/attached/degraded.
- Attachment revision fencing (drop stale hydration).
- whenAttached/whenDetached waiters.
- Timestamps come from new Date().toISOString(): millisecond precision with a Z suffix. Rust: chrono to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Millis, true). Go: t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z").

Cancellation uses chord Context (withCancel); map it to a CancellationToken / context.Context.

plugin.ts is the public plugin type surface: re-export the native traits.

Test support: experimental-durable-support.ts (openFauxConversation over MemoryStorage with the faux provider) is also used by the client-tui and plugin-reload tests in other units.

tasks.title: Experimental per-Session worker process, worker protocol, SessionWorkerManager, worker service composition
tasks.notes:
Worker protocol (session-worker.ts typebox):
- Commands and events use StrictObject (additionalProperties:false): #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] in Rust, json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields plus explicit validation in Go. Typebox also enforces integer/minimum constraints (instance.generation >= 1).
- Commands: shutdown, discover_workers, session_demand{serverConnectionId,requestId,attachmentId,attached}, operation{requestId, scope{serverConnectionId,attachmentId}, call{serviceId, instance?{key,generation}, member, args}}, operation_cancel.
- Events: worker_ready{token,sessionKey,sessionId,pid,metadata,pluginManifestPaths}, worker_failed, demand_applied, demand_rejected, operation_response{response: {type:"operation_result", result?} | {type:"operation_error", code?, message}}, service_update{scope, subscriptionId, update}.
- Optional fields must be omitted rather than serialized as null (skip_serializing_if / omitempty with pointer types).

Env vars:
- PI_SESSION_WORKER_CONTROL_ADDRESS, PI_SESSION_WORKER_CONTROL_TOKEN, PI_SESSION_WORKER_PEER_ID.
- PI_SESSION_WORKER_SESSION_KEY_BASE64 is Buffer.from(path).toString("base64url"), unpadded (Rust base64 URL_SAFE_NO_PAD, Go base64.RawURLEncoding).
- __PI_SESSION_WORKER_INITIAL_DEMAND_GRACE_MS (default 10000) and __PI_SESSION_WORKER_ORPHAN_DEMAND_GRACE_MS (default 30000).

WorkerLifecycle is a pure state machine (demand by attachment and generation, retirement holds while a demand ack is in flight, Harness activity, orphan and initial timers). Port it as a deterministic struct with an injectable clock and timers so the lifecycle tests can use fake time (vi.useFakeTimers equivalents: tokio::time::pause or a manual clock interface in Go).

The worker locks the Session dir with proper-lockfile: realpath:true, stale 2000ms, update 1000ms, retries 320 x 25ms, maxRetryTime 8000. The lock is the directory `<realpath>.lock`, its mtime is refreshed, and staleness is judged by mtime. Hand-port this for interop.

createCodingAgentHarness:
- ModelRuntime.create, SettingsManager.create(cwd), configureHarnessHttp, ExecutionEnvs.
- Harness.open on SQLite (rusqlite / modernc.org/sqlite), then findInitialAgentModel only when the root conversation is new.

SessionWorkerManager timeouts:
- startup 15s; shutdown 10s then SIGKILL; discovery 5s.
- Demand timeout 5s with compensation: send attached:false, and kill if that fails.
- No timeout on operations.

SessionWorkerManager bookkeeping:
- Subscription map key `${serverConnectionId}\0${attachmentId}\0${subscriptionId}`: use a tuple key natively.
- Pending calls are rejected on server replacement without stopping workers.
- SessionPluginSelectionConflictError when a different plugin selection targets a live Session.
- process.kill(pid,0) liveness and ESRCH handling.

services/worker.ts composes the builtin facets (agent-controller-runtime, session-plugins-runtime, models, transcript) and a plugin facet loader with reload/cutover. Natively the plugin loader becomes a registry of compiled-in facets; keep the reload generation semantics tested by experimental-plugin-reload.test.ts (the test uses an in-memory FacetLoader, so it is portable).

The lifecycle and manager tests use fake CoordinatorConnection objects and are fully portable.

tasks.title: Experimental server profile/activation/lifetime, Radius relay host+client transport, relay auth, plugin package profiles
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/experimental-presentation-facets.test.ts#builds conventional plugin entries into the server-owned plugin cache -- requires esbuild bundling of a TS plugin package (JS-only)

packages/coding-agent/test/experimental-presentation-facets.test.ts#builds the example plugin package without a package-owned build script -- builds examples/plugins/pi-example-plugin with esbuild (JS-only)
tasks.notes:
Server profile directory:
- Default ~/.pi/server, override PI_SERVER_DIR. It is created with mode 0700, and its owner must equal getuid(). Implement with nix/libc or x/sys/unix; on platforms without getuid it errors like TS.
- default-server-id is written with open flag wx (O_CREAT|O_EXCL), mode 0600. Its content must be a lowercase UUIDv4 (protocol isServerId); otherwise it is a corrupt-identity error. PI_SERVER_ID overrides it.
- Locks via proper-lockfile (hand-port):
  - launcher-<id>.lock: stale 30s, update 10s, retried every 25ms for up to 30s;
  - activation-<id>.lock: stale 20s, update 10s.
- plugin-packages-<id>.json is {"version":1,"packagePaths":[...]}: JSON.stringify(v,null,2)+"\n", mode 0600.
- session-plugin-packages-<id>-<sha256hex(sessionPath)[0:24]>.json is {version, sessionPath, packagePaths}.
- plugin-builds/<id>/<label>-plugin-<sha256hex(path)[0:12]>/.
- normalizePluginPackagePaths: path.resolve then dedupe, preserving first-seen order.

resolveSessionDirectory: default getAgentDir()/experimental/sessions; an explicit path gets ~ expansion and is resolved against cwd.

activateServer:
- Spawns role server with args [directory, serverId, sessionDir, JSON{provider?,model}?]. Keep the JSON key order.
- Polls connect every 10ms with a 10s timeout. Not-ready errors are ENOENT, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, EPIPE, ETIMEDOUT, DisconnectedError and ServerError code "version".

ServerLifetime: a foreground server has keepAlive. An auto server has a 10s startup grace and a 1s idle grace, and retires only when connections == 0 AND workers == 0. Port it as a pure struct with an injectable clock.

startServerBackend creates the pi-server unix listener with mode 0600. The serverNonce is randomUUID without dashes, first 12 chars.

Radius relay:
- URL: gateway origin + /v1/session-relays/<serverId>/connect, with https->wss and http->ws.
- Subprotocols pi-session-relay.host.v1 / pi-session-relay.client.v1; header authorization: Bearer <token>. Verify that the server-selected protocol matches.
- Host control JSON is {version:1, type: ping|pong|connection_open|connection_close, connection_id, code?}. The field name is snake_case connection_id. code must be in 1000-4999.
- Binary data frame: byte0 = version 1, byte1 = type 1, 16 raw UUID bytes, then the payload.
- connection_id regex: /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/u (lowercase v4 only).
- Backpressure: the pending bytes cap is 4 x 16 MiB. A drain wait polls bufferedAmount every 5ms until it is <= 1 MiB. tungstenite and coder/websocket expose no bufferedAmount, so track outstanding bytes in an OrderedWebSocketWriter equivalent (a single writer task with a byte-counted queue).
- Close codes: 4000 protocol error, 4001 transport error, 1012 when the server rejects the accept.
- Reconnect backoff doubles from 1s to 30s; it is 30s when unauthenticated.
- delay() uses unref'd timers. Natively, make sure the backoff sleeps are cancelled on close.
- Undici WebSocket error events can lack detail; the TS code synthesizes a useful message (the test asserts the text).

radius-auth:
- Explicit token or token file, else ModelRuntime OAuth provider "radius" with minOAuthValidityMs 5 min.
- PI_OFFLINE disables it.
- Exact error strings are in the summary hazards.

plugins/bundled.ts and plugins/package.ts are JS-only (esbuild build, then vm load). Natively, keep pluginBuildDirectoryName, profile read/write and normalization, but replace bundle building and loading with a compiled-in facet registry. createPresentationFacetData returns {presentationFacetBundles:[]} for native-only facets.

Tests:
- radius-relay tests use injected WebSocket factories plus allowNetwork() (vitest sets PI_OFFLINE=1 by default). Port them with an in-process WS server or a fake socket.
- presentation-facets tests 1-2 (reject local plugin paths for Radius servers; restore plugin package selections) are portable.
